jobs.title: Policy Program Manager, Safeguards Regulatory
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

As a Program Manager on Anthropic's Safeguards team, you'll help make sure we meet our obligations under AI safety laws and regulations around the world. Working closely with Legal, you'll turn new and emerging requirements into programs, controls, and deliverables. This requires a detailed understanding of how our models and products are built, evaluated and safeguarded. Your work will support Anthropic's commitment to developing AI safely and beneficially as the regulatory landscape evolves.

The responsibilities listed below are some examples of areas that someone in this role could own, depending on their experience and the team's needs.

Key Responsibilities

Manage and drive complex safety initiatives that identify, assess and mitigate risks from frontier models, from initial risk assessment through to the deployment of safeguards
Partner with the Safeguards incident management team to strengthen incident response and reporting processes, including the policies that determine how incidents are escalated and when they must be reported externally
Conduct post-incident reviews, and work with the subject matter experts for each harm area to incorporate the findings into model and product safeguards
Own the safety strategy and deliverables for AI systems used in high-risk settings, including risk assessments, technical documentation, and the information that deploying customers need to use those systems safely
Define the safety and risk controls that our models and products require, ensure that each control has an owner and a documented procedure, and confirm that it operates as intended
Partner closely with the owners of each risk area to develop a deep understanding of AI risks, safety evaluations and mitigation strategies, and use that understanding to prepare safety documentation, transparency reports and regulatory submissions

Minimum Qualifications

Experience in trust and safety, AI safety or a related field, including designing and implementing safeguards against misuse or harm
Understanding of AI safety, including the principal risk areas and the evaluations and safeguards used to address them, well enough to engage substantively with the technical experts responsible for them
Experience running risk assessment or harm mitigation programs from identification through to resolution
Experience translating policy or regulatory requirements into practical operational processes
Ability to drive complex, cross-functional programs to completion in a fast-moving environment, including with technical teams outside your own discipline
Clear written communication, including documentation for technical, legal and external audiences
Strong attention to detail, and the judgment to recognize when work is at risk and raise it early
Commitment to the safe development and deployment of AI

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with AI-specific regulation, such as the EU AI Act
Experience leading incident response programs, including escalation paths and external reporting obligations
Experience preparing safety documentation, transparency reports or regulatory submissions
Experience working with technical and research teams on safety evaluations

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary

$245,000—$285,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

As an Alaska Native owned corporation, our work helps secure an enduring future for our shareholders. Join our team and discover why we are a top veteran employer and Certified Great Place to Work™

ASRC Federal is seeking a Program Manager.

Advance readiness with ASRC Federal by leading a mission‑critical Defense logistics program supporting DLA Aviation. As the Program Manager
for Chemical Management Services (CMS), you will ensure safe, compliant, and uninterrupted delivery of hazardous materials vital to aircraft maintenance operations across multiple locations.

ASRC Federal’s Defense organization provides end‑to‑end chemical management, logistics integration, and mission sustainment support to key DoW customers. This program delivers hazardous material demand forecasting, procurement, warehousing, distribution, environmental compliance, and customer support for DoW aviation maintenance locations. You’ll lead a high‑impact team that keeps maintenance operations supplied and mission‑ready.

Key Responsibilities

As the Program Manager you will:

Serve as the primary customer interface, overseeing cost control, schedule performance, risk management, logistics analysis, and application of commercial best practices.
Establish program milestones, monitor adherence to master plans and schedules, identify performance issues, and drive resolution through resource allocation or contractual changes.
Coordinate development of proposals, business plans, operating budgets, statements of work, and contract terms/conditions.
Lead hazardous materials demand analysis, inventory forecasting, warehousing, receiving, storage, tracking, and delivery operations.
Ensure full environmental and safety compliance, including EPA/OSHA/DoD regulations and hazardous material handling standards.
Oversee employee training programs, ensuring workforce readiness and compliance with all hazardous material procedures.
Develop and manage a robust Quality Management System (QMS) and Quality Control Plan, including tracking Acceptable Performance Levels (APL) and driving continuous improvement.
Utilize Business Intelligence tools, Warehouse Management Systems (WMS), Inventory Management Systems (IMS), and Hazardous Materials/Environmental Management applications.
Build and sustain strong customer relationships with FRC leadership, DLA Aviation representatives, and other Government stakeholders.
Author, monitor, and report internal metrics, program plans, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
Identify opportunities to expand program scope, enhance services, and develop new Defense logistics capabilities.

Minimum Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in a related field.
Minimum 10 years’ experience managing resources and personnel for complex programs in a military government defense environment.
Experience with hazardous materials management.
Strong critical‑thinking skills, including root‑cause analysis and development of corrective actions.
Excellent communication skills and the ability to build strong relationships across all levels of Government customer leadership.
U.S. Citizenship, required for customer site and other accesses.

Desired Qualifications

Demonstrated leadership within DLA, DoW, or Defense logistics programs.
Experience implementing or managing QMS / ISO 9001 quality frameworks.
Proficiency with WMS/IMS and hazardous material inventory systems; proficiency with BI tools and reporting platforms.
Experience developing SOPs, metrics, and process improvement initiatives.
Ability to operate effectively in a mission‑driven, fast‑paced Defense logistics environment.

If you’re driven by operational excellence and ready to lead a high‑impact Defense logistics program, we’d love to have you on our team. Apply now and help ASRC Federal deliver safe, compliant, and reliable CMS support to its customers.

This opportunity is being advertised for proposal purposes only, the position is contingent upon contract award and customer approval of funding.

jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager, Global Supply Chain – LiDAR & Optical Circuit Switches (OCS)
jobs.description:
About us:

Voyant Photonics builds silicon photonic chips that steer and switch light at high speed. They power next generation, chip-scale FMCW LiDAR for robotics and autonomy, and optical circuit switches (OCS) for AI data centers. Based in NYC, we’re a hands-on team designing, building, and deploying frontier hardware to solve problems that matter, from how machines see to how AI scales.

The Role:

We're looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to build and run the global supply chain behind both of our product lines, LiDAR and OCS. You'll own supply chain programs from prototype sourcing through high-volume manufacturing. That means coordinating wafer foundries, packaging and test partners, component suppliers and contract manufacturers across North America, Asia and Europe. You'll work closely with engineering, operations, procurement, quality, finance and our customers to make sure we can build what we design, on time, at target cost and at scale.

Key Responsibilities

Supply chain program ownership: Lead end-to-end supply chain programs for LiDAR and OCS, covering sourcing strategy, supplier selection, capacity, cost targets and delivery schedules, all aligned to product NPI milestones.
Global supplier and partner management: Manage relationships with silicon photonics foundries, OSAT/packaging partners, contract manufacturers and key component suppliers (lasers, photodetectors, fiber arrays, micro-optics, MEMS, ASICs and PCBAs). Run quarterly business reviews and supplier scorecards, and support contract negotiations with procurement.
Demand and capacity planning: Run the sales and operations planning (S&OP) process. Translate customer forecasts from very different markets, such as robotics and industrial customers for LiDAR and hyperscalers for OCS, into wafer starts, assembly and test capacity, and inventory plans that account for long lead times.
NPI-to-volume transition: Drive manufacturing transfers, line qualification, yield ramps and second-source qualification as products move from prototype through EVT/DVT/PVT into mass production.
Supply risk and resilience: Identify and mitigate single-source, capacity, geopolitical and tariff risks. Build dual-sourcing strategies, buffer inventory plans and business continuity plans for critical parts.
Cost management: Own BOM cost roadmaps, should-cost models and cost-down programs. Track landed cost, including freight, duties and yield loss, against product cost targets.
Supplier quality and change control: Partner with quality engineering on supplier qualification, PPAP-style releases, product change notifications (PCNs), corrective actions (SCARs) and engineering change control across the supply base.
Logistics and trade compliance: Oversee global logistics, Incoterms, customs and country-of-origin requirements, and make sure export control and trade compliance obligations are met for both product lines.
Systems, metrics and process: Build and scale supply chain processes and tools (ERP/MRP, BOM management, supplier portals). Define and report KPIs such as on-time delivery, lead time, inventory turns, supplier yield and cost versus plan.
Executive and stakeholder communication: Give clear, concise status, risk and decision briefings to executives, the board, customers and cross-functional teams.

Core Values We Look For

Respect: We operate with humility and integrity, and we treat feedback as a gift.
Ownership: We own our achievements and our failures, and we step in to solve problems before anyone asks.
Simplicity + Clarity: We solve complex problems by building elegant, simple products and communicating clearly.

Required Qualifications

Education: Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Operations or a related technical field. MBA or Master's degree preferred.
Experience: 6+ years in technical program management, supply chain or operations for hardware products.
At least 5 of those years should be spent scaling complex hardware to volume production with global suppliers.
Semiconductor and photonics supply chain: Direct experience with wafer foundries, OSATs and contract manufacturers, ideally in photonics, optoelectronics or semiconductors.
Global supplier management: A proven record managing suppliers in multiple regions, including Asia, and leading commercial and technical discussions alongside procurement.
Planning and analytics: Strong command of demand and capacity planning, S&OP and ERP/MRP systems, with the ability to build data-driven models and turn them into decisions.
Program management rigor: Mastery of schedule, budget and risk management for cross-functional programs that span engineering, operations and external partners.

Nice to Have

Automotive and industrial supply chains: Experience with automotive or industrial quality and supply standards such as IATF 16949, AEC-Q qualification and APQP/PPAP, which are relevant to LiDAR customers.
Data center supply chains: Familiarity with hyperscaler supply requirements, customer supply agreements and data center qualification standards (e.g., Telcordia GR-468), which are relevant to OCS customers.
Optical component sourcing: Experience sourcing lasers, photodetectors, fiber assemblies, micro-optics, MEMS or other optoelectronic components.
Manufacturing quality systems: Hands-on use of PFMEA, control plans, change control and PCN management to keep a multi-tier supply base stable.
Trade compliance: Working knowledge of export controls, tariffs, country-of-origin rules and multi-region manufacturing footprints.
External test partners: Experience managing contract test houses, including test transfer, correlation and capacity planning.
Certifications and mindset: APICS/ASCM (CPIM or CSCP) or PMP certification is a plus. Comfort with ambiguity and a bias toward action in a fast-moving startup.

Life at Voyant

We build frontier hardware from our lab and office in Midtown Manhattan, where optical tables, lab benches and electronics sit alongside traditional office space. Our work is hands-on and primarily in person, but we don’t run on a rigid 9-to-5. We partner with customers across time zones, so some calls start early or run late, and we adjust schedules around them. We run a high-trust, high-accountability environment: you’ll own meaningful work, move quickly and often wear more than one hat. Voyant provides catered lunch every day at HQ, and we’re a diverse group of food lovers from around the world who enjoy sharing food, culture and technical ideas around the lunch table.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Voyant Photonics is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, pregnancy, marital or partnership status, age, national origin, citizenship, veteran or military status, disability, medical condition, genetic information, caregiver status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Compensation Range: $130K - $200K

Leadership

Scientific and Product Development expertise

Integrate regulatory, quality and IP/market considerations into project planning, risk anticipation and prioritization, ensuring strict adherence to compliance and ethical standards throughout the development lifecycle .

jobs.title: Policy Program Manager, Safeguards Regulatory
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

As a Program Manager on Anthropic's Safeguards team, you'll help make sure we meet our obligations under AI safety laws and regulations around the world. Working closely with Legal, you'll turn new and emerging requirements into programs, controls, and deliverables. This requires a detailed understanding of how our models and products are built, evaluated and safeguarded. Your work will support Anthropic's commitment to developing AI safely and beneficially as the regulatory landscape evolves.

The responsibilities listed below are some examples of areas that someone in this role could own, depending on their experience and the team's needs.

Key Responsibilities

Manage and drive complex safety initiatives that identify, assess and mitigate risks from frontier models, from initial risk assessment through to the deployment of safeguards
Partner with the Safeguards incident management team to strengthen incident response and reporting processes, including the policies that determine how incidents are escalated and when they must be reported externally
Conduct post-incident reviews, and work with the subject matter experts for each harm area to incorporate the findings into model and product safeguards
Own the safety strategy and deliverables for AI systems used in high-risk settings, including risk assessments, technical documentation, and the information that deploying customers need to use those systems safely
Define the safety and risk controls that our models and products require, ensure that each control has an owner and a documented procedure, and confirm that it operates as intended
Partner closely with the owners of each risk area to develop a deep understanding of AI risks, safety evaluations and mitigation strategies, and use that understanding to prepare safety documentation, transparency reports and regulatory submissions

Minimum Qualifications

Experience in trust and safety, AI safety or a related field, including designing and implementing safeguards against misuse or harm
Understanding of AI safety, including the principal risk areas and the evaluations and safeguards used to address them, well enough to engage substantively with the technical experts responsible for them
Experience running risk assessment or harm mitigation programs from identification through to resolution
Experience translating policy or regulatory requirements into practical operational processes
Ability to drive complex, cross-functional programs to completion in a fast-moving environment, including with technical teams outside your own discipline
Clear written communication, including documentation for technical, legal and external audiences
Strong attention to detail, and the judgment to recognize when work is at risk and raise it early
Commitment to the safe development and deployment of AI

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with AI-specific regulation, such as the EU AI Act
Experience leading incident response programs, including escalation paths and external reporting obligations
Experience preparing safety documentation, transparency reports or regulatory submissions
Experience working with technical and research teams on safety evaluations

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary

$245,000—$285,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. jobs.title: FMS Program Manager, Senior F-16 WAM (Secret)-205
jobs.description:
Overview

Overview

Join a team where innovation meets mission. Our AI, cloud, cyber, and modernization solutions save agencies thousands of hours, safeguard national security, and strengthen health and humanitarian missions worldwide. With more than 1,700+ team members, 1,500+ AI & data experts, and 100+ prime contracts, we deliver on a scale and with purpose.
We've been recognized as a Top Workplace by The Washington Post for six consecutive years and named to the Inc. 5000 list of Fastest-Growing Private Companies in 13 of the past 14 years. Credence is a welcoming environment for those looking to grow and make a meaningful impact. We encourage employees to push boundaries and help solve critical, world-changing federal challenges.
Position Summary

Credence has an immediate need for a FMS Program Manager who will be primarily responsible for supporting the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center WAM (AFLCMC/WAM) directorate, F-16 division at Wright Patterson AFB, OH. 
F-16 "Viper" AFLCMC/WAM is headquartered at Hill Air Force Base with units located at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Tyndall Air Force Base, Eglin Air Force Base, and Davis-Monthan Air Force Base.  The F-16 "Viper" is a multi-role fighter jet delivering air-to-air, air-to-ground, and surveillance capabilities for the United States Air Force (USAF) and Coalition Partners.
The F-16 program has the largest Foreign Military Sales (FMS) program in U.S. history producing over 4,500 jets for 24 countries.  Each F-16 FMS case is uniquely tailored to country requirements / development / funding.  Presently, FMS production orders exist through 2030. Additionally, the F-16 program includes the Multi-National Fighter Program (MNFP). MNFP is not a typical FMS program, but a unique, cooperative USAF and development program implemented through the FMS process under the framework of a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU). MNFP began in 1975 with the countries of Belgium, Denmark, the Netherlands, and Norway; Portugal joined in 200.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to the duties listed below:

Support the planning and organizing of program/project activities and analysis and perform professional or technical work related to program management.  The Contractor shall assist to plan, organize, complete, and present assessments of program/project management concepts, analyses, studies, and procedures.   The Contractor shall assist to evaluate implications of existing or proposed projects, programs, processes, and policies/laws and recommend improvements.
Provide support and technical expertise for various F-16 FMS programs in all DoD acquisitions stages to include planning, execution, delivery, sustainment and program closure IAW DoD policies and guidelines.
Provide support with the monitoring, reviewing, analyzing and coordination of security assistance issues concerning DoD and non-DoD agencies to ensure compliance with established policies, Letters of Request (LORs), and Letters Of Offer and Acceptance (LOAs), the Foreign Assistance Act, the Arms Export Control Act (AECA), and other relevant legislation. 
 provide support with the implementation and execution of assigned LOAs IAW the AECA, Security Assistance Management Manual (SAMM) as Defense Security Cooperation Agency (DSCA) Manual 5105.38-M and complete assigned projects with no or minimal assistance. 
Provide support with pre-LOA development, Statement of Objectives (SOO), SOW, and reviewing of weapon system Contractor proposals as assigned by the Government.
Assist with reviews of various documents, export licenses, or other documentation submitted by Contractors for Government review and assist with release and coordination of Government responses. 
Provide project management for FMS LOA and Manpower Requirements Package (MRP) modifications and amendments. 
Assist to analyze manpower needs for F-16 aircraft according to the LOR from country and LOA.
Assist to monitor the funding status and track expiring positions in coordination with Project Managers and Security Assistant Program Managers (SAPMs) to allocate and extend positions with country concurrence. 
Support SAPMs, line managers, and functionals across all phases of the acquisition process and assist to provide insight into areas relating to acquisition policy, streamlining, management, and lessons learned.

jobs.description:
The Company

Dexcom Corporation (NASDAQ DXCM) is a pioneer and global leader in continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). Dexcom began as a small company with a big dream: To forever change how diabetes is managed. To unlock information and insights that drive better health outcomes. Here we are 25 years later, having pioneered an industry. And we're just getting started. We are broadening our vision beyond diabetes to empower people to take control of health. That means personalized, actionable insights aimed at solving important health challenges. To continue what we've started: Improving human health.

We are driven by thousands of ambitious, passionate people worldwide who are willing to fight like warriors to earn the trust of our customers by listening, serving with integrity, thinking big, and being dependable. We've already changed millions of lives and we're ready to change millions more. Our future ambition is to become a leading consumer health technology company while continuing to develop solutions for serious health conditions. We'll get there by constantly reinventing unique biosensing-technology experiences. Though we've come a long way from our small company days, our dreams are bigger than ever. The opportunity to improve health on a global scale stands before us.

Meet The Team

At Dexcom, our Global Security team is redefining what it means to protect a mission-driven organization. We are more than a protective layer; we are embedded partners in innovation, culture, and care. We work shoulder-to-shoulder with teams across the company, utilizing secure-by-design principles, enabling innovation, safeguarding trust, and supporting the people who make life-changing technology possible.

This role isn’t just about security, it’s about leadership, partnership, and impact. You’ll join a team that’s building a modern, proactive security program rooted in strategy, prevention, collaboration, and service. We work cross-functionally, think globally, and act locally. If you’re energized by complexity, thrive in dynamic environments, and want to be part of a team that’s as mission driven as the company it protects, come join us!

Where You Come In

You lead security for Penang, translating Global Security priorities and site risks into operational objectives, staffing plans, service standards, and measurable outcomes.
You manage daily physical security operations, including contracted guard services, lobby and visitor operations, patrols, access control, CCTV, incident response, and event security.
You determine how site security resources are deployed to meet schedules, coverage requirements, service expectations, and short-term business goals.
You lead vendor governance, establish measurable service levels, validate staffing and invoices, and hold contracted providers accountable for training, quality, compliance, and corrective actions.
You lead site security risk assessments, incident reviews, audits, and remediation plans, escalating material risks with clear recommendations and business impact.
You serve as the site security lead during significant incidents and exercises, coordinating with site leadership, cross-functional partners, law enforcement, fire, and EMS.
You partner with Manufacturing, Facilities, EHSS, HR/ER, Legal, Data Privacy, IT, Quality, Supply Chain, and other functions to integrate security into site operations and change initiatives.
You oversee sensitive investigations support, including CCTV and access-control review, timeline development, evidence preservation, confidentiality, and chain of custody.
You establish site KPIs and provide concise reporting on risk, incidents, readiness, vendor performance, service delivery, corrective actions, and cost.

As the Security Manager for Penang, you are accountable for the performance and continuous improvement of the site security function. You lead through contracted security supervisors and personnel, influence across functions, manage resources and service delivery, and make risk-based decisions that protect employees, operations, assets, and business continuity.

What Makes You Successful

You bring broad knowledge of physical security operations and leading practices across guard force management, access control, CCTV, investigations, incident response, emergency preparedness, and audit readiness.
You have demonstrated management or team-lead experience, including setting objectives, allocating resources, coaching others, managing performance, and resolving complex operational issues.
You can manage outsourced security providers through clear service levels, staffing standards, performance reviews, corrective actions, and financial discipline.
You make sound, risk-based decisions in sensitive or rapidly evolving situations and communicate recommendations clearly to site leaders and functional managers.
You build productive partnerships across Manufacturing, Facilities, EHSS, HR, Legal, Data Privacy, IT, Quality, Supply Chain, and external stakeholders.
You use data, audits, incident trends, and stakeholder feedback to identify root causes, prioritize improvements, and measure results.
You have experience supporting security in manufacturing, medical device, technology, supply chain, or a similarly regulated operating environment.
You have working knowledge of Customs Trade Partnership Against Terrorism (CTPAT) supply-chain security requirements and Responsible Business Alliance (RBA) Code of Conduct expectations, including support for site assessments, audit evidence, corrective actions, and ongoing compliance.
You communicate effectively in English; proficiency in Bahasa Malaysia and other languages used at the site is strongly preferred.
Active participation in relevant security or resilience communities, and professional certifications such as CPP, PSP, PCI, CBCP, or equivalent credentials, are preferred.

What You’ll Get

A front row seat to life changing CGM technology. Learn about our brave #dexcomwarriors community.
A full and comprehensive benefits program.
Growth opportunities on a global scale.
Access to career development through in-house learning programs and/or qualified tuition reimbursement.
An exciting and innovative, industry-leading organization committed to our employees, customers, and the communities we serve.

jobs.title: Business Analyst, PMO (Release Excellence)
jobs.description:
Role Description

The Business Analyst - Release Excellence (AI Native) is an individual contributor within the PMO who helps make software releases more predictable, measurable, and ready for execution. You turn release data into clear insight, strengthen governance, improve recurring workflows, and give leaders and delivery teams a trusted view of readiness, risk, dependencies, and performance.

You will work across PMO, Product, Engineering, QA, DevOps, Support, and other stakeholders to improve how release information is captured, analyzed, reported, and acted on. You will use approved AI and automation tools where they create practical value - accelerating analysis, reporting, monitoring, and workflow execution while keeping validation and human accountability explicit.

You own the planning and governance layer of the release lifecycle - master release calendars, deployment scope, cut-over coordination, readiness reviews, release metrics, and release documentation - bridging development, QA, DevOps, and business stakeholders so updates ship safely, predictably, and with minimal downtime. This is not a release-engineering or engineering/product development role. You will not own software builds, deployment scripting, CI/CD engineering, source-control administration, or final production go/no-go decisions; you prepare and facilitate those decisions and coordinate rollback and incident follow-through with the accountable technical owners.

Key Outcomes

Release leaders and delivery teams have a timely, accurate, and consistent view of release readiness.
Risks, issues, dependencies, approvals, and exceptions are visible early and tracked to resolution or escalation.
Release metrics and dashboards are trusted, repeatable, and useful for decisions.
Manual reporting and governance administration decline through practical automation and AI-assisted workflows.
Release processes become more consistent through data-driven analysis, clear requirements, and measurable improvement actions.
AI-assisted outputs are validated, secure, appropriate, and traceable before operational use.

Roles & Responsibilities

Maintain accurate release-governance data across milestones, scope, readiness criteria, risks, issues, dependencies, decisions, approvals, exceptions, and action items.
Build and maintain the master release calendar, document deployment scope, and coordinate cut-over windows and branching decisions across multiple cross-functional teams.
Coordinate Go/No-Go readiness reviews and change and technical review boards (CRB/TRB) - assembling evidence, tracking entry and exit criteria, capturing decisions, and publishing outcomes - while final approval authority remains with accountable owners.
Map technical dependencies ahead of each release, confirm rollback and contingency plans are documented and agreed with engineering, and coordinate triage and follow-through when deployments fail or post-release defects surface.
Track release health metrics such as deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, and mean time to restore, and drive continuous-improvement actions from the resulting trends.
Maintain the release documentation set - deployment instructions, release notes, runbooks, disaster-recovery and rollback references, and cross-team status communications.
Build and maintain release dashboards, readiness views, recurring reports, and analytical summaries that provide clear visibility into delivery health and release performance.
Analyze readiness trends, schedule movement, defect and quality signals, dependency aging, exception patterns, deployment outcomes, and other release indicators to identify emerging concerns and improvement opportunities.
Prepare evidence for release-readiness reviews, governance checkpoints, and leadership discussions. Organize facts, open items, risks, and decision needs without assuming final approval authority.
Track cross-team dependencies and unresolved blockers, identify aging or execution gaps, and support timely escalation to accountable owners.
Partner with Release Excellence leadership and cross-functional teams to define metric definitions, reporting standards, data-quality rules, readiness criteria, and governance artifacts.
Document current-state processes, identify bottlenecks and recurring manual work, and translate findings into clear business requirements, workflow changes, acceptance criteria, and measurable improvement actions.
Support release retrospectives and recurring operational reviews by synthesizing data, themes, root causes, actions, and follow-through.
Use approved AI tools to accelerate reporting, summarization, risk sensing, dependency analysis, and process analysis. Validate outputs against trusted source data before use.
Identify repeatable PMO and release-governance activities that can be automated or converted into controlled workflows, including reminders, evidence collection, approval tracking, status preparation, and recurring reporting.
Maintain decision logs, governance records, and audit-relevant documentation, so release activity is traceable and accessible.
Partner with technical teams to understand release signals and constraints while preserving the role boundary between business analysis and technical release engineering.
Communicate clearly across technical and business audiences, surfacing facts, tradeoffs, risks, and required decisions in a concise and actionable way.
Contribute to the Release Excellence operating model by improving standards, templates, measures, workflows, and governance practices over time.

Education

Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Systems, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, Engineering, Analytics, or a related STEM field, or equivalent practical experience.

Experience(years including)

3 to 8+ years of experience in business analysis, software release management, configuration management, project or program analysis, PMO operations, software delivery, release coordination, quality operations, or a related technical analyst role.
Working knowledge of the software development lifecycle (SDLC), CI/CD pipelines, Git version control, and cloud environments such as AWS or Azure.
Experience working in a software development lifecycle environment with Engineering, QA, Product, DevOps, or adjacent delivery teams.
Experience building reports, dashboards, process documentation, requirements, or governance artifacts from operational data.
Experience tracking risks, issues, dependencies, milestones, actions, and cross-functional delivery commitments.
Experience with Agile or Scrum delivery environments. Exposure to scaled delivery models is helpful.
Experience using AI, workflow automation, or advanced reporting tools to improve analysis, documentation, monitoring, or operational processes is preferred.

Skills

Business analysis and requirements definition.
Release readiness and delivery analytics.
Release planning, scheduling, and cut-over coordination.
Change and release governance facilitation, including CRB/TRB and Go/No-Go readiness reviews.
Risk assessment, conflict resolution, and cross-functional negotiation.
Data validation, reconciliation, and metric definition.
Dashboarding, reporting, and executive-ready synthesis.
Risk, issue, dependency, and action tracking.
Process mapping, root-cause analysis, and continuous improvement.
Workflow automation and AI-assisted productivity.
Agile / Scrum and SDLC fluency.
Stakeholder communication and facilitation.
Governance documentation and decision traceability.

Abilities

Turn complex delivery data into concise, decision-ready insight.
Work across teams without direct authority and maintain disciplined follow-through.
Distinguish facts, assumptions, risks, decisions, and recommendations clearly.
Identify patterns and process weaknesses without losing sight of operational context.
Challenge inconsistent data or unclear process steps constructively.
Balance speed, quality, governance, and practical delivery needs.
Learn technical release concepts well enough to analyze signals and ask effective questions without taking on release-engineering ownership.
Maintain accuracy and composure when release timelines are compressed or information is changing quickly.

Tools & Technologies

Agility or Jira for work, release, risk, dependency, and status tracking.
Azure DevOps, ServiceNow, Jenkins, GitLab, or equivalent Agile, ITSM, and pipeline tooling.
Git-based source control and AWS or Azure cloud environments at a working-familiarity level.
Confluence or equivalent collaboration and documentation platforms.
Dashboarding and analytics tools used by the organization.
Microsoft 365 or equivalent productivity and reporting tools.
Approved generative AI and AI-assisted analytics tools.
Workflow automation tools used for notifications, approvals, evidence collection, and recurring PMO processes.
Working familiarity with CI/CD concepts, source control, deployment pipelines, testing workflows, and environment progression sufficient to interpret release information; hands-on engineering ownership is not required.

AI Usage and Accountability Requirements

Use only approved AI tools and follow organizational requirements for confidentiality, security, data handling, and responsible AI use.
Validate AI-generated summaries, analyses, risk signals, recommendations, and stakeholder communications against trusted source information before operational use.
Do not treat AI output as approval, evidence, or a final decision without appropriate human review.
Maintain traceability for material AI-assisted analysis when it informs release governance, escalation, or leadership communication.
Use AI to reduce repetitive effort and improve analytical consistency while preserving human judgment for exceptions, tradeoffs, escalation, and recommendation quality.
Escalate suspected AI errors, data-quality issues, inappropriate outputs, or governance concerns.
Keep final ownership with accountable people. AI may support a release decision, but it does not own go/no-go, risk acceptance, production change approval, or stakeholder accountability.

Success Measures / Accountable Outcomes

Accuracy and timeliness of release-readiness reporting.
Completeness and quality of release-governance data and decision records.
Reduction in manual effort required to prepare recurring release reports and governance artifacts.
Visibility and aging of unresolved risks, issues, dependencies, approvals, and actions.
Adoption and consistency of release metrics, readiness criteria, and reporting standards.
Quality and usefulness of analytical insights provided to Release Excellence leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.
Completion and measurable impact of process-improvement and automation initiatives within assigned scope.
Evidence that AI-assisted outputs are reviewed, validated, and used in accordance with governance requirements.
Contribution to improving release predictability, readiness transparency, and operational discipline over time.

AI Competency Alignment & Proficiency Expectations

Target Proficiency: Intermediate for the competencies below.
Generative AI Reporting and Documentation - independently develops release and governance updates using approved generative AI tools, improves clarity and stakeholder relevance, and uses AI-assisted summaries to streamline reporting workflows.
AI-Powered Delivery Performance Monitoring - analyzes routine release and delivery trends using AI-assisted monitoring tools and uses predictive indicators to identify potential risks or bottlenecks.
Predictive Risk and Issue Management - uses AI-assisted monitoring to identify emerging concerns, supports mitigation tracking, and maintains structured risk and issue records.
AI-Assisted Dependency Management - manages routine dependency tracking with AI-assisted planning tools, identifies dependency risks or execution gaps, and supports milestone coordinatio

jobs.title: Senior Threat Intelligence Analyst
jobs.description:
Position: Senior Threat Intelligence Analyst

Work Location: Reston, VA (Hybrid)

Reports To: Threat Intelligence Officer, Americas

Travel Required: Up to 10% Domestic Travel

Job Status: Full-Time, Exempt

OUR CULTURE

At FS-ISAC, how we work matters as much as what we do. We believe in:

Strengthening collaboration across FS-ISAC, its membership, and strategic partners.
Teamwork and collective success.
Humility and curiosity to grow, learn, and continuously improve.
Role modeling a culture of open, constructive feedback – both giving and receiving.  
Acting with integrity and accountability, upholding our policies, and making principled decisions that reflect our commitment to doing what is right. 

Position Summary 

The Threat Intelligence Analyst III is a senior cybersecurity professional responsible for leading complex cyber threat intelligence analysis and producing high-impact intelligence products that support the security and resilience of the global financial sector. This role independently researches advanced threats, threat actors, cyber campaigns, geopolitical developments, and emerging risks to deliver actionable intelligence and strategic insights.

Working with minimal supervision, the analyst serves as a trusted advisor to members, leadership, and industry partners; leads intelligence initiatives; supports organizational strategy; and mentors’ junior analysts while advancing intelligence-sharing efforts across the financial sector.

Essential Job Duties

Lead complex intelligence investigations involving cyber threat actors, ransomware operations, nation-state activity, vulnerabilities, and emerging threats.
Collect, correlate, and analyze intelligence from technical and non-technical sources.
Produce tactical, operational, and strategic intelligence assessments for members and stakeholders.
Analyze adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) and map findings to frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK.
Assess the impact of cyber incidents, geopolitical developments, technology trends, and systemic risks affecting the financial sector.
Author intelligence reports, threat assessments, alerts, white papers, and executive briefings.
Present intelligence findings and risk recommendations to executives, members, and external partners.
Translate technical intelligence into actionable business and risk-management insights.
Lead information-sharing initiatives, intelligence exchanges, and member engagement activities.
Build and maintain relationships with financial institutions, government agencies, law enforcement, and industry partners.
Represent the organization at conferences, webinars, and industry forums.
Leverages AI to enhance analysis, decision-making, productivity, and innovation. Maintains awareness of emerging AI technologies, threats, and risks.
Contribute to intelligence strategy, collection priorities, and analytical standards.
Identify opportunities to improve intelligence methodologies, workflows, automation, and reporting capabilities.
Lead cross-functional projects and support organizational cyber resilience initiatives.
Mentor Threat Intelligence Analyst I and II team members and provide analytical coaching and product reviews.
Promote best practices in intelligence collection, analysis, reporting, and information sharing.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Security, Computer Science, Intelligence Studies, International Affairs, Criminal Justice, or a related field
8+ years of experience in cyber threat intelligence, intelligence analysis, cybersecurity, incident response, threat hunting, or related disciplines
Advanced knowledge of cyber threat intelligence methodologies and intelligence lifecycle management
Deep understanding of threat actors, cybercrime ecosystems, nation-state operations, malware, ransomware, vulnerabilities, and threat hunting concepts
Experience assessing cyber risk, identifying trends, and developing actionable intelligence products
Advanced knowledge of AI-enabled tools and technologies relevant to the role. Ability to independently conduct complex intelligence analysis and investigations
Knowledge of Threat Intelligence Platforms (TIPs)
Intelligence automation and enrichment tools
Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) research methodologies
Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) technologies
Threat hunting platforms
Malware analysis tools and techniques
Scripting and analytical tools (e.g., Python, PowerShell, SQL)
Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills
Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, including experience briefing executive audiences
Ability to influence stakeholders and provide strategic intelligence guidance
Demonstrated leadership, collaboration, and mentorship capabilities
Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, PowerPoint, and Word
Must be able to obtain and maintain a Top Secret (TS/SCI) security clearance

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting financial services, critical infrastructure, government, military, intelligence, or cybersecurity organizations preferred.
Experience leading intelligence projects and presenting to executive audiences.
Certified Threat Intelligence Analyst (CTIA)
GIAC Cyber Threat Intelligence (GCTI)
GIAC Certified Incident Handler (GCIH)
CompTIA Security+
Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
SANS/GIAC certifications or equivalent threat intelligence certifications
Certified Ethical Hacker (CEH)
Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE)
Association of Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialists (ACAMS)

WORK ENVIRONMENT

This is a hybrid position that reports to Reston, VA headquarters (up to four days per week in office). Employees are expected to maintain a professional work environment and be able to perform the essential functions of the role. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these functions. This job description is intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed and is not an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, or skills required. Job duties may be modified or assigned as business needs evolve.

Compensation And Pay Transparency Disclosures

Full-Time Annual Salary Range: ($155,000-$185,000 USD) Individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to, business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience.

Incentive Compensation: This position is eligible to participate in the organization’s discretionary annual incentive/bonus plan subject to plan terms in addition to individual and organizational performance.

Benefits: Medical, dental, vision, life insurance, disability coverage and accident insurance, 401(k) with employer match, paid time off, paid holidays, parental leave, along with other types of leave, and professional development opportunities. Other incentives may be available based on position level.

jobs.description:
Remote location: United Kingdom.
Minimum qualifications:

Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
5 years of experience working in a government or military environment, leveraging and developing Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) for network, host, and log analysis to enable the detection of and response to cyber threats.
Experience leveraging CTI data and tooling to describe, track, and develop new intelligence on Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs).
Experience analyzing network data, Intrusion Detection System (IDS) monitoring, Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) solutions, and contributing CTI into a threat intelligence platform.

Preferred qualifications:

Experience in the analysis of CTI, supporting monitoring, detection, and response capabilities.
Experience in deploying and analyzing data from technical security controls (e.g. web proxy, firewalls, IPS, IDS, enterprise antivirus solutions, network analyzers).
Experience with standard network logging formats, network management systems and network security monitoring systems, and security information and event management.
Experience in SOC operations, threat hunting, detection engineering and SOC workflow optimization.
Active UK Developed Vetting (DV) Security Clearance.

About The Job

In this role, you will join Mandiant Intelligence as an Advanced Intelligence Access (AIA) Integrator, delivering key support to a strategic UK government client, embedded onsite four days per week, serve as a Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) technical specialist, empowering the customer and becoming a key contributor to their mission.

You will join a fantastic team, backed by Mandiant’s UK and global experts, supported with training, specialisms, access to industry-leading tooling and proprietary data to fuel your analysis. In this role, you will blend this unparalleled reach with your own technical tradecraft, driving capability maturity via automation and platform engineering to help secure UK Public Sector, and deliver impactful CTI for cyber defense.

Part of Google Cloud, Mandiant is a recognized leader in dynamic cyber defense, threat intelligence and incident response services. Mandiant's cybersecurity expertise has earned the trust of security professionals and company executives around the world. Our unique combination of renowned frontline experience responding to some of the most complex breaches, nation-state grade threat intelligence, machine intelligence, and the industry's best security validation ensures that Mandiant knows more about today's advanced threats than anyone.

Responsibilities

Embed onsite at the customer location (3-4 days/week), partnering to support their Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) requirements and integrate deeply to enable their focused cyber defense mission.
Track priority cyber threats as an embedded CTI centre of expertise, applying frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK, and leveraging Mandiant tools and data to answer customer Request for Information (RFI's), author actionable intelligence and support dissemination and briefings.
Support the integration of CTI into the customer's mission by building processes for its application within varied cyber defence technology stacks, including SIEM and TIP systems (Splunk, netflow, Sigma, Yara etc).
Leverage Google Threat Intelligence Platform and other customer sources to maximise exploitation of CTI in Threat Hunting, with a focus on network analysis.

jobs.description:
Job Description

Tiered Approach

In Line With The Commitment To Safeguard Capacity And Support Personnel Already In The Organization, a Majority Of UNDP UNCDF/UNV Vacancies Are Advertised Using a Tiered Application Process Whereby

Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.
Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments
Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers
Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

In 2025, the National Council of Justice (CNJ) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) established a partnership aimed at promoting innovation in cybersecurity for the Brazilian Judiciary. Project BRA/25/025 develops and implements tools and strategies to strengthen cybersecurity, digital preservation and information integrity, expanding the protection of the Judiciary’s systems and users.

The initiative strengthens institutional security and promotes transparency, good governance and the efficiency of judicial processes, contributing to resource savings and to a more agile Justice system for the benefit of citizens and society.

To this end, the project governance is organized into the following fronts:

Four Cross-cutting Coordination Axes

General Coordination;
Integrated Monitoring and Control Unit;
Technical and Operational Management Unit;
Training and Communication Unit;

Four Workstreams, Focused On

Regulatory compliance;
Operational conformity;
Network governance;
Promotion of a cybersecurity culture;

As this is a home-based position, the candidate is expected to have adequate working conditions, including the infrastructure and equipment necessary for the full performance of the activities.

Duties And Responsibilities

The Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst will be assigned to the Network Governance axis and will be responsible for leading the collection, analysis and dissemination of cyber threat intelligence, with the aim of anticipating risks, enriching the understanding of incidents and threat actors, and strengthening the resilience of Judiciary institutions within the context of project BRA/25/025.

The incumbent will work in close coordination with the CNJ and UNDP teams, and the following indicative activities are foreseen:

Cyber Intelligence Coordination and Dissemination

Engage in the threat information-sharing network among Judiciary bodies, ensuring the smooth flow of tactical and operational data.
Produce intelligence inputs for operational alerts, threat advisories, and rapid dissemination bulletins for technical teams and managers.
Facilitate cooperation with national and international Computer Security Incident Response Teams (CSIRTs) and public sector cooperation networks.
Contribute to a proactive, forward-looking cyber defense posture for the Judiciary, anticipating threats based on the intelligence produced and shared.
Support the operation and curation of intelligence-sharing platforms (e.g., MISP, OpenCTI), using standards such as STIX/TAXII and the Traffic Light Protocol (TLP) for the classification and dissemination of information.

Intelligence Production and Threat Analysis

Conduct advanced analyses of threat actors, their motivations, capabilities and TTPs (Tactics, Techniques and Procedures), applying analytical models such as the Diamond Model and the Cyber Kill Chain.
Transform raw data from technical, open and internal sources into actionable intelligence to support proactive defense and improve incident containment, observing operational security (OPSEC) best practices in collection activities.
Support vulnerability prioritization based on the actual likelihood of exploitation in the current threat landscape.
Monitor open sources, forums, deep and dark web channels, and national and international technical reports to identify campaigns, data leaks and threats targeting the public sector and the Judiciary.
Define, maintain and periodically review Priority Intelligence Requirements (PIRs), ensuring intelligence production remains aligned with organizational risks, priorities and the evolving threat landscape.

Strengthening Proactive Detection

Produce and provide indicators of compromise (IoCs), behavioral patterns and detection signatures/rules (e.g., YARA, Sigma, Snort/Suricata) to feed monitoring systems (SIEM, EDR, IDS/IPS, etc.).
Collaborate with Blue Team, Threat Hunting and Incident Response teams to validate intrusion hypotheses based on threat intelligence.
Assess the effectiveness of security coverage against techniques mapped in frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK, identifying detection gaps and proposing adjustments.
Support the automation and orchestration of intelligence workflows (collection, enrichment, correlation and distribution), integrating CTI platforms with SOAR and monitoring tools.
Support the analysis of incident-related artifacts, logs and relevant technical evidence to extract relevant IoCs and TTPs.

Strategic Risk Management and Security Posture

Contribute to periodic security posture reviews with an external view of threats specifically targeting the public sector and the Judiciary.
Identify long-term cyberattack trends to guide investments and changes in the defense architecture.
Propose improvements to technical controls based on the evolution of identified threats.
Support External Attack Surface Management (EASM) activities by identifying exposed assets, leaked credentials and indicators of organizational exposure.

Integration with Capacity Building and Innovation

Integrate real-world threat intelligence into Situational Awareness programs to raise user maturity against targeted attacks.
Promote the use of CTI frameworks (e.g., MITRE ATT&CK, Diamond Model, Cyber Kill Chain), OPSEC best practices and security data analysis.

Continuity, Reporting and Simulations

Participate in the development of realistic threat scenarios for crisis simulation exercises and continuity plans.
Produce technical intelligence reports, threat assessments, and executive summaries tailored to technical teams and senior management.
Conduct workshops and training on intelligence analysis for local teams.

Knowledge Management

Document analysis methodologies and lessons learned from relevant incidents, and keep the knowledge base on sector adversaries up to date.
Develop and maintain analytical templates, reporting standards and intelligence production guidelines to ensure consistency across the intelligence lifecycle.
Promote the reuse of intelligence products across Incident Response, Threat Hunting, Vulnerability Management and Security Operations teams

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Project.

Institutional Arrangement

The incumbent will be supervised by the Governance and Network Management Analyst.

Competencies

Core competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Direction & Strategy | Strategic Thinking:

Develop effective strategies and prioritized plans in line with UNDP’s objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, potential risks and opportunities; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight

Business Direction & Strategy | Business Acumen:

Ability to understand and deal with a business situation in a manner that is likely to lead to a good outcome. Ability to make good judgments and quick decisions within such frameworks in the organization. Knowledge and understanding of the operational frameworks in the organization.

Business Development | Human-centered Design:

Ability to develop solutions to problems by involving the human perspective in all steps of the problem-solving process. Knowledge and understanding of human-centered design principles and practices.

Business Management | Project Management:

Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management.

Digital | Cyber and Data Privacy Security Risk Management:

Ability to anticipate, prepare for and respond to potential Risks and issues that may results in Data breaches that can cause potential identity theft and personal harm and can also negatively impact UNDP's reputation

2030 Agenda: Peace | Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights:

Effective Justice Sector Institutions

2030 Agenda: Peace | Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights:

Access to Justice

Required Skills And Experience

Min. Education requirements:

Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in Information Security, Information Technology, Information Systems, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Telecommunications Engineering, Electrical Engineering or related fields is required, or
A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Min. Years Of Relevant Work Experience

Applicants with Master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience.
Applicants with a Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of two (2) years of experience in Cyber Threat Intelligence.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section:

Recognized complementary training in CTI, OSINT, OPSEC, digital forensics or related areas.
Previous experience in a Security Operations Center (SOC), CSIRT/CERT or dedicated threat intelligence team, preferably in the public sector or the justice system.
Experience in collecting and analyzing open-source intelligence and in using cyber threat intelligence platforms (e.g., MISP, OpenCTI).
Experience using scripting and query languages (e.g., Python, KQL, SPL) for collecting, parsing and analyzing large volumes of security data.
Experience in writing technical and executive reports on cyber threats.
Experience with the Brazilian legal and regulatory framework on cybersecurity and data protection.

Required Language(s)

Fluency in Portuguese is required.
Fluency in English is desirable.

jobs.description:
Job Summary

We are seeking a Research Operations Analyst
to support a multi-year mineral title consolidation program for one of the largest royalty funds in the United States.

This is a program-scale, long-term engagement
that spans the full retitling pipeline- from title research through revenue recovery
. The role begins with a strong focus on chain-of-title research
, but is designed as an entry point into a broader operational career path across adjacent functions including curative resolution, owner communications, recording operations, and revenue administration
.

The ideal candidate combines the analytical rigor of a legal researcher
, the precision of a data analyst
, and the operational adaptability
to learn and execute across evolving workflows.

Key Responsibilities

Conduct structured chain-of-title research for owner/fund pairs, tracing ownership histories from current ownership back to origin.
Review and interpret legal documents including deeds, probate filings, court orders, affidavits, conveyance instruments, and powers of attorney.
Cross-reference ownership data across multiple sources (county records, ownership registers, transfer histories) to verify accuracy and identify discrepancies.
Identify and document title gaps, ownership defects, missing documents, inflated decimals, and chain breaks, and flag issues for review and resolution.
Classify ownership records using the program's A/B classification framework (clean title vs. curative required).
Enter research findings into structured databases using defined workflows and validation protocols.
Assemble and maintain complete evidence packs, including supporting documents, source references, and classification rationale, with proper version control.
Ensure all research outputs meet quality standards, targeting a 90%+ first-pass acceptance rate, and participate in quality control audits.
Navigate and extract data from county clerk and recorder systems across multiple jurisdictions, adapting to varying formats and access methods.
Use land records aggregator platforms where direct county access is limited or incomplete, and document county-specific access constraints.
Maintain consistent productivity against defined throughput benchmarks, with improving efficiency over time.
Follow established research methodologies, SOPs, and workflow protocols, and incorporate feedback to continuously improve accuracy.
Cross-train into additional operational functions over time, including curative resolution, owner communications, recording operations, operator engagement, and revenue transition workflows, following structured training and competency assessments.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Law, Business, Finance, Political Science, Public Administration, or a related field.
Strong analytical and research skills with exceptional attention to detail and ability to maintain accuracy across high-volume work.
Ability to read, interpret, and extract information from legal and property-related documents.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook) and comfort working with structured databases.
Strong written communication skills to document findings, flag issues, and assemble structured evidence files.
Ability to manage multiple workflows simultaneously while maintaining organization and meeting productivity targets.
Self-disciplined, reliable, and comfortable working within structured processes and defined methodologies.
Strong learning agility and adaptability as responsibilities expand across the operational pipeline.
Fluency in English is required; French, Arabic, or Urdu is a plus.

Nice to Have

Experience in title research, legal research, land records, real estate transactions, or property administration.
Familiarity with U.S. county records systems, land data platforms, or document aggregator services.
Understanding of property ownership structures, mineral rights, or chain-of-title concepts.
Experience in data entry, document review, or compliance-driven environments with quality standards.
Exposure to oil & gas operations, royalty administration, or mineral interest management.
Experience working in cross-functional, distributed teams across multiple time zones.

The Information Security Analyst, Security Trust supports security assurance workflows across the Information Security organization. This includes customer security reviews, Trust Center operations, third-party risk assessments, vendor security reviews, security documentation, evidence management, and operational reporting.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys analyzing security information, communicating clearly, improving processes, and using artificial intelligence tools to reduce manual work. This is an on-site position in our St. Louis, MO office.

Are you someone who can look at business performance, spot what others may be missing, and use data to uncover what is driving the results?

The Operations Business Analyst reports to Recovery Operations and serves as a shared analytical resource across Recovery Operations, Operational Excellence, and Finance. This role uses business analysis, operational data, and Power BI to identify performance changes, bottlenecks, discrepancies, risks, and opportunities that require action.

You will build and maintain operational dashboards that make business performance visible, but the role goes well beyond reporting. You will investigate what the data is telling us, determine why performance is changing, identify where processes or results are breaking down, and provide clear, actionable insights that help business leaders determine where action is needed.

The ideal candidate combines strong business judgment with hands-on analytical capability. You can build a Power BI dashboard, but more importantly, you know what to look for, what questions to ask, and how to turn what you find into meaningful business insight.

Identify Performance Issues & Opportunities

Monitor operational and financial performance to identify bottlenecks, discrepancies, trends, risks, and emerging opportunities.
Analyze productivity, inventory quality, throughput, recovery performance, capacity, cycle time, and financial results.
Conduct root-cause analysis to understand why performance is improving, declining, or deviating from expectations.
Identify issues that may require operational, process, workflow, or technology changes.
Translate findings into clear, actionable insights for business leaders.

Build Performance Visibility

Develop and maintain Power BI dashboards and reports that provide meaningful visibility into business performance.
Define, monitor, and analyze KPIs that measure operational effectiveness and financial outcomes.
Analyze data across multiple sources to identify discrepancies, relationships, and performance drivers.
Improve reporting consistency, data quality, and metric integrity.
Develop focused analyses when existing dashboards or reporting do not fully explain business performance.

Measure Business Impact

Establish baselines and measures of success for operational and process improvements.
Evaluate the impact of workflow changes, process improvements, and automation initiatives.
Determine whether implemented changes are producing the intended operational and financial results.
Develop scenario analyses, forecasts, and performance projections to support business decisions.
Identify new risks, opportunities, or performance issues revealed by changing results

Partner Across the Business

Work closely with Recovery Operations, Operational Excellence, and Finance to investigate business performance and surface opportunities for improvement.
Provide the analysis and insights needed to help leaders prioritize where action is required.
Partner with Operational Excellence by providing the data, root-cause analysis, and performance insights needed to inform process and solution design.
Communicate findings clearly to both operational and executive audiences.
Follow improvements through implementation to measure results and identify additional opportunities.

Qualifications
