Manage and drive complex safety initiatives that identify, assess and mitigate risks from frontier models, from initial risk assessment through to the deployment of safeguards
Partner with the Safeguards incident management team to strengthen incident response and reporting processes, including the policies that determine how incidents are escalated and when they must be reported externally
Conduct post-incident reviews, and work with the subject matter experts for each harm area to incorporate the findings into model and product safeguards
Own the safety strategy and deliverables for AI systems used in high-risk settings, including risk assessments, technical documentation, and the information that deploying customers need to use those systems safely
Define the safety and risk controls that our models and products require, ensure that each control has an owner and a documented procedure, and confirm that it operates as intended
Partner closely with the owners of each risk area to develop a deep understanding of AI risks, safety evaluations and mitigation strategies, and use that understanding to prepare safety documentation, transparency reports and regulatory submissions

Minimum Qualifications

Experience in trust and safety, AI safety or a related field, including designing and implementing safeguards against misuse or harm
Understanding of AI safety, including the principal risk areas and the evaluations and safeguards used to address them, well enough to engage substantively with the technical experts responsible for them
Experience running risk assessment or harm mitigation programs from identification through to resolution
Experience translating policy or regulatory requirements into practical operational processes
Ability to drive complex, cross-functional programs to completion in a fast-moving environment, including with technical teams outside your own discipline
Clear written communication, including documentation for technical, legal and external audiences
Strong attention to detail, and the judgment to recognize when work is at risk and raise it early
Commitment to the safe development and deployment of AI

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with AI-specific regulation, such as the EU AI Act
Experience leading incident response programs, including escalation paths and external reporting obligations
Experience preparing safety documentation, transparency reports or regulatory submissions
Experience working with technical and research teams on safety evaluations

We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

The Business Operations team sits within Finance and partners across Chainalysis to strengthen how the company plans, makes decisions, and executes. Combining analytical rigor with practical operating judgment, the team helps leaders translate company priorities into clear plans, effective operating rhythms, and measurable outcomes. As Chainalysis continues to evolve, Business Operations also helps build the processes and ways of working that enable teams to scale and adapt.

You’ll join a close-knit team working with partners across Finance, R&D, go-to-market, Legal, Security, and beyond. The team takes on high-priority work across the business, often creating structure where approaches are still taking shape, and helps teams align and move change forward. This role offers broad exposure to Chainalysis and the opportunity to help shape how the company operates through its next stage of growth.

In this role, you’ll:

As a Senior Business Operations Analyst at Chainalysis, you will be a strategic operator and connective tissue across leadership and functions - helping translate company priorities into clear plans, operating rhythms, and measurable outcomes. You’ll partner with leaders across Finance, Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and other teams to improve how the business plans, makes decisions, and executes.

You’ll support high-priority, cross-functional initiatives end to end: framing ambiguous problems, developing analyses and recommendations, aligning stakeholders, establishing milestones and governance, and driving follow-through. You’ll help run planning and business review cadences, build KPI reporting and insights, improve processes and systems, and support change initiatives such as pricing and packaging, go-to-market readiness, product launches, and organizational or operating-model changes.

You will also:

Identify friction in cross-functional workflows and design scalable processes, tools, and operating mechanisms.
Prepare clear, data-informed recommendations and executive-ready materials.
Manage multiple work-streams and facilitate alignment across stakeholders, balancing speed, rigor, and effective change management.

We are looking for candidates who have/are:

3–6 years of experience in business operations, strategy and operations, management consulting, finance, program management, or a related field—ideally in a SaaS or technology environment.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate data into insights, recommendations, and decisions.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to create executive-ready narratives and materials.
Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives from problem definition through implementation and measurable outcomes.
Strong project and program management skills, including prioritization, stakeholder management, and attention to detail.
Familiarity with business intelligence, data, and collaboration tools; experience with Jira, Confluence, Databricks, spreadsheets, SQL, and/or AI-powered tools is a plus.
Ability to drive clarity in ambiguity, influence without authority, and demonstrate resilience in a dynamic environment.
Curious, adaptable, and motivated to learn quickly, challenge assumptions, and make the company and team better.

Nice to have experience:

Business Operations or Strategy & Operations experience in a high-growth SaaS or technology company.
Supporting annual or quarterly planning, operating cadences, business reviews, resource allocation, or strategic planning processes.
Establishing KPIs, building performance dashboards, and using data to identify trends, risks, and opportunities.
Supporting pricing and packaging, go-to-market or commercialization initiatives, product launches, or broader change-management efforts.
Applying agile, lean, or other process-improvement methodologies to scale how teams work.
Interest in and general knowledge of blockchain and cryptocurrency, including key players and market dynamics.

AI at Chainalysis

AI is not a feature at Chainalysis - it is a new way of working. One that turns instructions into work done, and helps us move faster than the threats we're built to counter, and we expect our employees to take ownership of the output and ensure quality. As the world's most trusted blockchain analytics platform, Chainalysis sits at a rare intersection of proprietary data, regulatory relationships and crypto expertise that makes it uniquely placed to shape and lead the next era of AI-driven intelligence - and we expect everyone here, regardless of role, to be an active part of it.

Our mission is to build trust in blockchains, blending safety and security with an unwavering commitment to growth and innovation.

You belong here.

Analyse business data and translate findings into clear, actionable insights.

jobs.title: Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Our Company
The North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) is a not-for-profit international regulatory authority whose mission is to assure the effective and efficient reduction of risks to the reliability and security of the grid. NERC develops and enforces Reliability Standards; annually assesses seasonal and long‐term reliability; monitors the bulk power system through system awareness; and educates, trains, and certifies industry personnel. NERC’s area of responsibility spans the continental United States, Canada, and the northern portion of Baja California, Mexico. NERC is the Electric Reliability Organization (ERO) for North America, subject to oversight by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) and provincial authorities in Canada. NERC’s jurisdiction includes users, owners, and operators of the bulk power system, which serves nearly 400 million people.

Our Mission
The vision for the ERO Enterprise, which is comprised of NERC and the six Regional Entities, is a highly reliable and secure North American bulk power system. Our mission is to assure the effective and efficient reduction of risks to the reliability and security of the grid.

Your Impact
The Senior Data Analyst, Reliability Assessment, applies technical skill, experience, and subject-matter expertise in the areas of data management and analysis to support the ERO’s efforts to independently assess and report on the overall reliability, adequacy, and associated risks to the interconnected North American bulk power system. This Senior Data Analyst role includes responsibilities to collect, process, and analyze data necessary for assessing risks that could arise from the growing reliance on natural gas for electricity generation, with application to resource adequacy and bulk power system reliability assessments.

The Senior Data Analyst is part of the reliability assessment team that provides superior technical analysis and designs ERO processes for developing and publishing NERC’s reliability assessment reports, including the Long-Term Reliability Assessment and seasonal assessments. The Senior Data Analyst coordinates with the Performance Analysis team to provide reliability assessment information and analysis for the State of Reliability report and the Data and Analytics Integration team on data management, data quality, and analysis.

The Senior Data Analyst, Reliability Assessment, reports to the Manager, Reliability Assessments.

Your Role
Working with members of the reliability assessment team, analyze and interpret energy supply and infrastructure information, including: electricity generation, load, and transmission system data; and natural gas supply and infrastructure data.
Develop data requests and manage timely collection of reliability data from NERC registered entities to support the identification of electric reliability risks in NERC reliability assessments, with a focus on risks related to interdependent electric-natural gas energy systems.
Develop, implement and manage approaches, methods, and processes to promote data quality and reduce potential for data errors following best practices on data management.
Support the transformation of complex data into visualizations for use in NERC reliability assessments products.
Collaborate with NERC and ERO Enterprise subject matter experts that manage and use various reliability data systems on projects to make systems more compatible and interoperable.
Make use of available datasets containing generation, load, transmission, and natural gas fuel supply information to augment NERC’s collected data in analyzing trends and emerging risks to electric reliability.
Proactively identify and suggest solutions to technical analysis and data problems.
Develop working knowledge of the fundamentals of NERC Reliability Assessments.
Develop, implement and adhere to policies, procedures, and processes for the collection, storage, safeguarding, and authorized dissemination of data.
Support internal coordination with the Performance Analysis, Event Analysis, Engineering, Standards, and Compliance teams, as needed.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

The successful candidate will have at a minimum:

BS in Engineering, Economics, Statistics, Data Analytics, Computer Science, Information Management, or similar combination of education and training.
Previous experience within the energy sector performing a regulatory, monitoring, or analysis role.
Familiarity with publicly available historical energy data sets (EIA, DOE, FERC, Natural Gas Pipeline Electronic Bulletin Boards (EBBs), etc.) as well as any pertinent proprietary data sets.
Intermediate-level computer and programming skills in applications such as Python, Microsoft SQL Server, and Excel (i.e., Macro, VBA, PowerPivot).
Exceptional interpersonal and communications skills, both oral and written.
Strong critical thinking and analytical skills and attention to detail.
Capability to work both independently and collaboratively on teams and support multiple tasks concurrently.

Preferred candidates will also have:

Advanced degree and professional certifications or credentials.
Understanding of roles and responsibilities for North American bulk power system owners and operators.
Proficiency in writing for technical and general audiences.

Other

A background check will be conducted prior to employment.
In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification document form upon hire.
This position has been classified as exempt.
The position may be based remotely but must be able to travel to NERC offices or meeting locations when needed. Reimbursement of travel expenses will be in accordance with the company’s travel and expense reimbursement policies.

Our Culture Declarations

Everyone at NERC is a leader.
We are accountable personally and organizationally to deliver on commitments.
We develop ourselves and people in the organization to ensure that NERC realizes its strategic objectives.
We are resilient and adaptable to the challenges and needs of the business and our team.
We exude a growth mindset and empower teams to take risks.
We build collaborative relationships within NERC, the ERO, and the stakeholders of NERC.
We exemplify NERC cultural behaviors:
Reward high-quality, creative, and innovative work
Attract, engage, and retain top talent
Value and respect diverse perspectives
Provide a safe, inclusive, and collaborative work environment
Form strong relationships within the company, and with the ERO Enterprise
We demonstrate curiosity in a wide variety of areas and are open to exploring new situations, knowledge, and opportunities for growth and development.
We demonstrate an anticipatory mindset, preventing problems and building contingencies where appropriate.
We are champions for diversity and inclusion, seeking out and values diverse perspectives.
We value well-being, prioritizing collaboration, engagement, and connection among our team.

jobs.title: Data Analyst – Power BI
jobs.description:
AST SpaceMobile is building the first and only global cellular broadband network in space to operate directly with standard, unmodified mobile devices based on our extensive IP and patent portfolio and designed for both commercial and government applications. Our engineers and space scientists are on a mission to eliminate the connectivity gaps faced by today’s five billion mobile subscribers and finally bring broadband to the billions who remain unconnected.

Position Overview

We are seeking a Data Analyst – Power BI to join the Enterprise Applications Data Team. This role owns the design, development, security, and documentation of AST’s Power BI reporting across manufacturing, HR, and leadership functions. Working closely with business owners, IT Security, and the MES/ERP teams, the Data Analyst turns data from Tulip MES, NetSuite ERP, Rippling, SharePoint, and the enterprise data lake into trusted, governed dashboards that support operational and executive decision-making. The role also enforces AST’s Power BI Dashboard Development standards — group-based access, service-account connections, row-level security, and complete documentation — and helps scale self-service analytics across the company.

Key Responsibilities:

Design, build, publish, and maintain Power BI reports, dashboards, and semantic models for the AST & Science Global, AST Leadership, Midland HR, and Midland Manufacturing workspaces.
Partner with the named Business Owner of each report to gather requirements, define KPIs and metric definitions, and validate data accuracy before anything is published to production.
Build dimensional (star-schema) data models, DAX measures, and Power Query transformations; write targeted SQL queries that extract only the data required — never full-table loads.
Source and integrate data from Tulip MES, NetSuite ERP, Rippling, SharePoint/Excel, and the enterprise data lake, consuming curated silver and gold layers and working with data engineering on the bronze/silver/gold (medallion) design.
Work with the MES and architecture teams to define reporting data points so Tulip tables capture the fields needed for manufacturing KPIs such as work-order progress, step durations, cycle time, and efficiency.
Implement Row-Level and Object-Level Security (RLS/OLS) based on the ISA-95 scope block (legal entity, site, area, work center) and functional domains, using Microsoft Entra ID security groups only — no individual user access.
Configure data connections with approved service accounts or service principals, with credentials managed in 1Password; manage gateways and scheduled refresh to remove dependencies on individual user accounts.
Apply Power BI workspace governance: admin group at creation, role-based workspace access, App-based distribution, and Contributor enablement so trusted business users can build self-service reports from published datasets.
Produce and maintain the required documentation for every report — Architecture Overview (ARCH), Data Source Details (DS), Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), Access & Security (ACCESS), and Issue Log (ISSUE) — so any team member can support it without help.
Diagnose and resolve refresh failures, credential issues, and data-quality problems; perform root-cause analysis and work requests through the Enterprise Applications Jira queue.
Optimize report and model performance (e.g., incremental refresh, query folding, model size reduction) and recommend improvements to the reporting platform.
Train and support business users and Contributors on Power BI usage, standards, and self-service best practices.
Support ad-hoc analysis and executive reporting requests for operations, manufacturing, HR, and leadership stakeholders.

Qualifications

Education:

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, Data Analytics, Statistics, Industrial Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Experience:

A minimum of 5 years of experience as a Data Analyst, BI Developer, or similar role, including at least 3 years of hands-on Power BI development in an enterprise environment.
Strong SQL skills (joins, CTEs, window functions, query optimization) against relational databases or data warehouses.
Proven experience with Power BI Desktop and Service: data modeling, DAX, Power Query, workspaces, Apps, gateways, scheduled refresh, and RLS.
Experience building ETL/ELT pipelines and integrating data from multiple enterprise systems (ERP, MES, HRIS, SaaS, files).
Experience defining and tracking operational KPIs and translating business questions into measurable, documented metrics.

Preferred Qualifications:

Microsoft Certified: Power BI Data Analyst Associate (PL-300); Fabric Data Engineer Associate (DP-700) a plus.
Experience in manufacturing, aerospace, or another regulated production environment; familiarity with OEE, yield, throughput, and cycle-time reporting.
Experience with MES and ERP data, especially Tulip and NetSuite.
Experience with cloud data platforms such as Azure (Data Factory, Data Lake, Azure SQL), Microsoft Fabric, Snowflake, or AWS (S3, Glue, Apache Iceberg).
Experience with service principals / Azure AD app registrations, Power BI deployment pipelines, and Git-based version control.
Working knowledge of Python for data preparation, automation, or forecasting.
Exposure to AI-enabled analytics (e.g., Copilot in Power BI, anomaly detection, forecasting).

Soft Skills:

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with meticulous attention to data accuracy.
Ability to translate technical concepts for non-technical audiences and present findings clearly to executives.
Proven ability to collaborate across Manufacturing, HR, Finance, IT Security, and Enterprise Applications teams.
Documentation discipline — treats documentation as part of the deliverable, not an afterthought.
Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and deliver in a fast-paced, rapidly changing environment.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Technology Stack:

Power BI Desktop, Power BI Service, DAX, Power Query (M), Power BI Apps and gateways.
SQL / T-SQL; Python (preferred).
Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) security groups and service principals; 1Password.
Data sources: Tulip MES, NetSuite ERP, Rippling, SharePoint, Excel, enterprise data lake.
Microsoft 365 (Excel, Teams, SharePoint), Jira, Visio.

A cover letter and resume are required for consideration for this position; include the cover letter as the first page of your application. The letter should specifically address your interest in this position and outline relevant skills and experience.

Job Summary

The Demography of Aging, Disability and Care Program (DADC) in the Survey Research Center at the Institute for Social Research (ISR) conducts research focused on the consequences of population aging. The program provides leadership for several research projects including the National Health and Aging Trends Study (NHATS) and the National Study of Caregiving (NSOC).

We are seeking a full-time social science data analyst intermediate to collaborate with DADC research faculty to conduct analyses related to population aging, disability and care. The successful candidate will specialize in quantitative social science and have experience working with population-based aging-related surveys, like the National Health and Aging Trends Study (NHATS) and the National Study of Caregiving (NSOC) or similar national surveys.

This is a two-year term limited position with the possibility of extension. An extension will be based on available funding and performance. This position will report to the DADC program director.

Responsibilities*

The job functions of this role will include, but are not limited to:

35% Preparing survey data and creating analytic files

Writing programs to clean, recode and handle missing survey data using statistical packages such as Stata or R.
Prepare and organizes data files for statistical analysis.

35% Performing statistical analyses

Uses a variety of statistical methods and models. Selects and runs statistical tests in consultation with research faculty. Includes weighted analysis of descriptive data and model estimation, including generalized linear models (e.g., linear, logistic, and count regression), survival analyses, and mixed models. Advanced techniques like machine learning methods that may require deeper knowledge of R or Python are also of interest.

30% Documenting procedures and preparing methodological and technical materials

Clearly documents decisions including analytic file construction, variable generation, and model estimation.
Collaborate with research faculty to contribute technical material to publications and presentations. May include descriptions of data and methods, including design decisions, sample size justification, and analytic approach, and well-notated tables and figures.

Required Qualifications*

Master's degree in social science or public health field (e.g., epidemiology, quantitative sociology, demography, health services), or related field.

Highly motivated, organized, detail-oriented person with excellent multi-tasking ability and record-keeping.
Must be able to program, manage data, and conduct statistical analyses using statistical software packages such as Stata or R.
Willingness to learn and apply new methods and approaches.
Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, including ability to document complex data management and statistical work and excellent interpersonal skills.

Desired Qualifications*

Experience with the National Health and Aging Trends Study (NHATS) and National Study of Caregiving (NSOC)

jobs.description:
We anticipate the application window for this opening will close on - 21 Oct 2026

Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact.

A Day in the Life

Peripheral Vascular Health (PVH) is a dynamic business with annual revenue exceeding $1 billion across multiple high-growth therapy areas. PVH focuses on diagnosing and treating diseases of the peripheral arteries and veins, helping patients restore blood flow and reduce the risk of limb loss and other serious complications. The portfolio includes minimally invasive technologies such as drug-coated balloons, stents, atherectomy, thrombectomy, embolization, vein ablation, and embolic protection, designed to address complex peripheral vascular disease across a range of patient anatomies. By combining innovation, clinical evidence, and physician partnership, PVH aims to improve procedural outcomes and quality of life for patients worldwide.

At Medtronic, we bring bold ideas forward with speed and decisiveness to put patients first in everything we do. This position is remote to enhance our competitive edge and expand our cross-functional collaboration efforts. This role will require 10% of travel to enhance collaboration and ensure successful completion of projects.

The Senior Health Economics & Outcomes Research (HEOR) Analyst
will be a critical contributor on the Cardiovascular HEOR team. The Senior HEOR Analyst is responsible for providing analytical and methodological expertise to support the development and execution of global health economic and outcomes evidence for Cardiovascular products, with an emphasis on the Peripheral Vascular Health portfolio. This position may be called upon to support multiple therapies, with a specific focus area on leading the execution of studies using administrative data to generate regulatory-grade evidence.

Role and Responsibilities:

Designs and conducts studies using administrative health care claims data and device-derived data to assess outcomes, health services utilization, treatment patterns and costs associated with the use of PVH therapies. Analysis may be used to support evidence development, federal and global agency (FDA, CMS, EU MDD/MDR) requests, clinical trial design, and reimbursement market trends.
Designs and conducts observational and economic research studies that provide value, perspective and evidence for clinical and/or pre-clinical product portfolio decisions, marketing, regulatory agency submissions, and product reimbursement strategies.
Compares and evaluates the value of products and therapies with the clinical, economic, and quality of life outcomes data from clinical trials and/or epidemiology studies, registries, observational studies, modeling, surveys, and meta-analysis.
Prepare observational and economic research study results for dissemination via abstract, presentation, and/or peer-reviewed publication.
Develops country specific evidence to meet requirements for optimal reimbursement coverage and usage.
Works closely with Reimbursement staff to determine the global economic evidence needs and potential impact of evidence on therapy coverage, payment, and adoption.
Works with clinical research to add relevant health outcomes and economic endpoints to clinical trials and biostatisticians to analyze and report study results.

Must Have; Minimum Requirements

Baccalaureate degree
Minimum 4 years of relevant experience in healthcare industry working with health care data (medical device, pharmaceutical, biotech, insurance, hospital, health system) or advanced degree and 2 years of post-graduate experience in healthcare industry working with health care data (medical device, pharmaceutical, biotech, insurance, hospital, health system) preferred

Nice To Have

Advanced degree in health policy, health services research, health economics, epidemiology, or related field of study
Experience working with administrative claims data
Experience designing, modifying, or implementing decision analysis models (i.e., cost-effectiveness, budget impact)
Experience working with large databases including health care claims, administrative, or patient discharge data as a health service researcher, epidemiologist, data programmer or economist
Proficiency programming using statistical software (e.g. SAS, STATA, R, etc.)
Demonstrated competency in database file manipulation, data analysis and graphical presentation
Strong quantitative skills, preferably with training in econometrics or statistics
An understanding of health insurance and the U.S. health care system
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, especially the ability to communicate complex analytical techniques in a way that is understandable by non-quantitative audiences
Experience in the development of regulatory-grade analysis, synthesis, and presentation of complex data from multiple sources
Project management experience; demonstrated consultative mindset
Proven ability to work effectively in a highly matrixed organization
Proven relationship-building and maintaining skills with internal and external stakeholders including physician customers, hospital administrators or payers

214.2(h)(4)(iii)(A) is required.

Analyzes data to inform strategic ministry choices, making those ministries more effective.
Develop new and actionable research approaches to answer key ministry questions.
Produce documentation, trainings, reports, presentations, etc. for methods and projects.

Experience with product innovation frameworks and processes as well as user experience testing.
Understanding of research and data tools including: Qualtrics, Decipher, Excel, SPSS, JMP etc.Ability to create methods and deliverables that do not have organizational precedent Able to work with and lead volunteers as they make themselves known to the Crossroads Insights Team.

Join us in bringing joy to customer experience. Five9 is a leading provider of cloud contact center software, bringing the power of cloud innovation to customers worldwide.

Living our values everyday results in our team-first culture and enables us to innovate, grow, and thrive while enjoying the journey together. We celebrate diversity and foster an inclusive environment, empowering our employees to be their authentic selves.

At Five9, we believe every customer interaction should be effortless, connected, and on brand. To help us deliver on that vision, we’re hiring a Senior Creative Project Manager—a detail-obsessed, process-driven project manager who shepherds creative and content projects from kickoff to delivery and is often the last set of eyes on an asset before it goes live — ensuring every asset reflects our visual identity and brand voice.

In this role, you’ll manage the day-to-day execution of creative and content assets—coordinating across teams, optimizing workflows, and serving as the final checkpoint for both visuals and messaging. You’ll review creative and content for accuracy, consistency and alignment with Five9 tone, voice and style guidelines, and route issues back to the right owner to fix. You’ll partner closely with content and creative teams while managing and continuously improving the intake, tracking and workflows that bring it all together.

This is a hands-on, senior individual contributor role for someone who brings equal parts operational discipline and creative judgement — and who understands that great brand experiences depend on both.

We are focusing on AI tools across the team, and this role will help us use them well, safely, and on brand.

Key Responsibilities

Own and improve creative request and production processes, identifying opportunities to streamline intake, prioritize competing requests, enforce intake standards and scale output

Identify bottlenecks early, escalate risks and suggest solutions to keep work moving
Lead creative calls, check-ins, and debriefs when needed
Keep stakeholders in the loop without overloading the creative team
Capture lessons learned in project debriefs and keep process documentation, templates, and QA checklists current
Use AI tools like Claude to speed up everyday work such as briefs, status updates, QA checks, and process documentation
Review AI-assisted content and visuals with the same care as everything else, checking for accuracy, tone, and brand fit before anything goes live

Understanding of graphic design fundamentals (layout, typography, color, and file formats)
Excellent organizational and time management skills; strong communicator who works well with creatives and stakeholders alike
Calm under pressure, flexible with shifting priorities, and always two steps ahead
A team player who cares about process, quality, and the people doing the work
Hands-on experience using AI tools like Claude in daily work, including writing clear prompts and getting reliable results
Familiarity with AI image and video tools, and good judgement about when AI helps and when a person needs to take over

Experience managing budgets and opening/maintaining Pos
Experience working in or with an in-house creative team or agency, including vendor management and agency collaboration

jobs.description:
About Us

Ethos Risk Services is a leading insurance claims investigation and medical management company committed to providing better data that translates into better decision-making for our clients. We are at the forefront of innovation in our space, and our success is driven by a dynamic team passionate about delivering exceptional services to our customers.

Job Summary

Ethos' Product Management team is seeking a full-time Program Manager, M&A Integration (REMOTE)
to own acquisition integration from end to end. Every company we acquire brings systems, data, and people that need to be absorbed quickly and cleanly. This role owns the planning, the acquired-company relationships, the execution, and the escalations, and turns each migration into a repeatable playbook so every integration after it is faster and less costly. The role also coordinates cross-team dependencies across four product lines, maintains the portfolio view of initiatives, milestones, and risks, and delivers concise executive status reporting.

Our ideal candidate is a seasoned program manager who has run M&A integrations or large-scale system migrations and is comfortable starting with an ambiguous mandate and closing it themselves.
There is no formal PMO at Ethos today, so the practices this person builds become it. This is a high-autonomy role for someone who manages complex, multi-stakeholder programs with minimal oversight and can distill status into one page an executive can act on.

Key Responsibilities

Integration Ownership - Own acquisition integration programs end to end, including scoping, planning, timelines, resourcing, risk management, and delivery.
Acquired-Company Partnership - Serve as the primary point of contact for acquired-company stakeholders through migration, managing communication, expectations, and change management.
Playbook Development - Codify each migration into a repeatable integration playbook with templates, checklists, data-migration runbooks, and lessons learned, so integration costs decline over time.
Portfolio Management - Coordinate cross-team dependencies across four product lines and maintain a portfolio view of initiatives, milestones, and risks.
Executive Reporting - Produce concise executive-level status reporting and escalate only true decision points, with options and a recommendation attached.
Process Improvement - Identify and remove process bottlenecks and establish lightweight program-management practices that add speed, not overhead.

Qualifications

Education:
Bachelor's or Master's degree in business, management, or a related field (preferred). Equivalent professional experience may be a substitute for higher education/

Experience

Minimum of 7 years of program or project management experience (required).
Minimum of 2 years running M&A integrations, large-scale system migrations, or comparable multi-stakeholder programs (required).
Experience with data and systems migration programs (required).
Experience with claims, healthcare, insurance, or similarly regulated data (strong plus).
Background in insurance, workers' compensation, medical case management, or healthcare services (preferred).
Experience standing up program-management or PMO practices from scratch in a growing company (preferred).
Familiarity with product-led organizations and agile delivery (preferred).

Certifications

PMP, PgMP, or equivalent certification is welcome but not required. Results matter more than credentials.

Skills

Demonstrated ability to own a complex program independently, from ambiguous mandate to delivered outcome, with minimal oversight (required).
Strong stakeholder management, including experience working with external or newly acquired organizations (required).
Excellent written communication, with the ability to distill program status into one page an executive can act on (required).

Working Conditions

This is a remote position based in the United States, working in a home office environment. The role requires frequent prolonged periods of a stationary position and constant operation of a computer and other office productivity equipment. Occasional travel is required.

jobs.title: Business & Transformation Program Manager
jobs.description:
At Franklin Templeton, we believe success is built through powerful partnerships. As a forward thinking asset manager, we build dynamic relationships with clients, understand their goals, and navigate complex markets together. We leverage cutting edge strategies and deep insights to unlock opportunities for long term wealth creation. Our talented, global teams bring expertise that is both broad and unique.

From our welcoming, inclusive, and supportive culture to our globally diverse business, we offer opportunities not only to help you reach your potential, but also to contribute to our clients’ success.

About The Department

The Enterprise Business Strategies & Implementation team serves as the execution engine for Franklin Templeton's most important strategic priorities. Working directly with the Co-Presidents, Executive Leadership Team, and senior business leaders, the team shapes and drives complex enterprise initiatives that advance the firm's strategy. Team members act as trusted advisors and transformation leaders, partnering across Investment Management, Distribution, Technology, Operations, Legal, Compliance, Finance, Marketing, Human Resources, and Corporate Services to solve complex business challenges, influence decisions, and deliver measurable strategic outcomes. Employees gain direct exposure to executive leadership and the opportunity to lead work that shapes the future of a global asset manager.

How You Will Add Value

Enterprise Strategy & Execution

Lead the execution of the firm's highest-priority business strategies and enterprise initiatives.
Translate executive vision and strategic priorities into clear roadmaps, decisions, and measurable outcomes.
Advise executive sponsors, challenge assumptions, and drive timely decisions at the highest levels of the firm.
Develop recommendations and decision frameworks for executive leaders navigating complex business opportunities and challenges.
Anticipate business risks, opportunities, dependencies, and enterprise-wide impacts before they affect delivery.

Enterprise Program Leadership

Lead complex business transformation programs, applying consulting-style problem solving, executive advisory skills, and strategic decision support from strategy through execution.
Establish governance, decision-making, and accountability models that enable senior leaders to act quickly.
Independently lead multiple high-impact initiatives with limited oversight and competing priorities.
Evaluate business, operational, financial, legal, regulatory, and technology implications through an enterprise lens.
Create momentum, remove barriers, and drive execution with urgency, sound judgment, and disciplined follow-through.

Executive Partnership

Serve as a trusted strategic advisor to executive leadership and senior business stakeholders.
Develop concise, decision-oriented executive communications, recommendations, and briefing materials.
Lead executive workshops, strategic planning sessions, and governance forums that move decisions forward.
Develop and communicate informed points of view, challenge assumptions constructively, and drive executive decisions.

Cross-Functional Leadership

Build strong partnerships across functions, businesses, and regions to advance enterprise priorities.
Influence executives and senior leaders without direct authority, including when viewpoints or priorities differ.
Create alignment across complex stakeholder groups and translate competing perspectives into a clear path forward.
Promote accountability, transparency, collaboration, and enterprise-minded decision-making.

Change Leadership

Lead the people and business dimensions of enterprise transformation and organizational change.
Operate effectively through ambiguity, independently determine next steps, and maintain momentum.
Quickly develop expertise in unfamiliar business topics and structure ambiguous challenges into actionable recommendations.
Identify opportunities to strengthen operating models, governance, efficiency, and enterprise execution.

What Will Help You Be Successful In This Role

Extensive experience leading large-scale business strategy, transformation, or enterprise initiatives.
Demonstrated experience advising executive leadership and influencing senior-level decisions.
Experience independently leading cross-functional initiatives across complex, matrixed organizations.
Management consulting, corporate strategy, business transformation, or comparable enterprise leadership experience strongly preferred.
Strong business acumen and the ability to quickly understand unfamiliar issues, form a point of view, and recommend action.
Exceptional executive communication, relationship-building, and stakeholder management skills.
Proven ability to influence without direct authority, challenge constructively, and drive accountability through execution.

Technical Skills

Business strategy development and enterprise program leadership.
Executive advisory, decision support, and senior-level communications.
Business transformation, operating model, and strategic initiative execution.
Organizational change leadership and stakeholder alignment.
Enterprise governance, risk assessment, and decision-making frameworks.
Financial analysis, business case development, and outcome measurement.
Structured problem-solving and consulting methodologies.
Familiarity with AI tools such as Copilot and ChatGPT to accelerate project planning, meeting follow-up, executive summaries, and related strategic work products.

Work Schedule & Location

This is a hybrid role that can be based out of Stamford (CT), Boston (MA), New York City (NY), Short Hills (NJ), Washington (DC), Baltimore (MD), Fort Lauderdale (FL), West Palm Beach (FL), or St. Petersburg (FL), with an expectation of three days onsite per week. The position follows a 37.5-hour workweek, with standard working hours of 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET.

Compensation

Franklin Templeton offers employees a competitive and valuable range of total rewards - monetary and non-monetary - designed to support their well-being and recognize their time, talents, and results. Along with base compensation, employees are eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, a 401(k) plan with a generous match, and recognition rewards. We also offer a comprehensive benefits package, which includes a range of competitive healthcare options, insurance, and disability benefits, employee stock investment program, learning resources, career development programs, reimbursement for certain education expenses, paid time off (vacation / holidays / sick / leave / parental & caregiving leave / bereavement / volunteering / floating holidays) and a motivational wellbeing program. We expect the annual salary for this position to range between $150,000 - $200,000, depending on location and level of relevant experience, plus discretionary bonus.

#MID_SENIOR_LEVEL

At Franklin Templeton, we believe your benefits should support your life, your goals, and your future. That’s why we offer a comprehensive Total Rewards package designed to help you thrive both personally and professionally.

Highlights Of Our Benefits Include

Paid Time Off: Three weeks of PTO in your first year
Health Coverage: Competitive medical, dental, and vision insurance to support your well-being
Retirement Savings: 401(k) plan with an 85% company match on pre-tax and/or Roth contributions, up to IRS limits
Equity & Investing: Employee Stock Investment Plan (ESIP) with discounted share purchase opportunities
Learning Education Assistance Program (LEAP): To support your ongoing growth and career advancement
Employee Investment Benefits: Opportunity to purchase company funds with no sales charge

new_jobs.title: Project Manager (MEP Engineering)
new_jobs.description:
Miller-Remick is a full-service MEP engineering firm looking for energetic, self-motivated, and innovative individuals to join our team. If you think you are a good fit for this role, we encourage you to apply.

We are looking for a Project Manager that can demonstrate the successful delivery of multi-discipline design packages on capital projects ranging from $5M to $100M, coordinating teams that include structural, mechanical, and electrical engineers and designers. This position may be filled anywhere in the US.

In addition to the basic qualifications listed, the successful candidate shall possess the skills required to successfully develop and execute project tasks and deliverables, be a collaborative team player, manage multiple complex tasks simultaneously, establish and manage priorities, and have a strong drive to deliver a quality project for customers.

Our clients include federal agencies (e.g. Department of Veterans Affairs, Department of Defense, General Services Administration, and the Federal Bureau of Prisons), as well as state and local governments. Projects have varied degrees of complexity and a wide range of estimated construction costs and include new construction and renovations of hospitals, healthcare and military facilities, federal office buildings and courthouses, state and local government buildings, research laboratories, corrections facilities and site utility infrastructure projects.

Responsibilities and Requirements:

Project management functions include scope responsibilities, client management, scheduling, and financials.
Lead and manage projects from planning through design and construction.
Lead project team meetings and report project status to executive management.
Complete internal peer reviews and provide input in multi-discipline page turns, across all offices, to assist in the development of a comprehensive design.
Perform page turns prior to all major project deliverables.
Work closely with subconsultants and department design managers.
Assist in developing client capture plans and pursuit plans, proposals, and other business development and client engagement activities.
Develop and enhance client relationships, serve as the primary company contact, and deliver quality projects on time, within budget, and to the satisfaction of the client.
Administer relevant aspects of a formal quality program.
Marketing and business development support to include the identification of potential business opportunities.
Work with the leadership team to develop fees on complex projects.
Develop and maintain client relationships.

Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Structural Engineering, or Electrical Engineering.
At least 10 years of engineering experience, including a minimum of 4 years of experience as a PM.
PE, PMP, and/or equivalent license is preferred.
Experience in the healthcare and/or government contracting markets preferred but not required.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to perform project management responsibilities, working independently and in coordination with other team members and Project Managers.
Ability to manage multiple projects with multiple clients at varying stages of design/construction completion.
Travel as required to client sites.

Miller-Remick does not provide visa sponsorship or support. Candidates are required to successfully complete a federal background check for security clearance.

The anticipated salary range for this position is $130,000 - $170,000 annually. Actual compensation will be determined based on several factors, including experience, qualifications, education, certifications and licensure.

About Miller-Remick

We are a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business committed to supporting our brave military and veterans through a comprehensive array of consulting engineering and construction management services with a focus on leadership, quality, and responsiveness.

In addition to a competitive salary, our employees enjoy a full benefit package including medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401k with matching, PTO, and 12 paid holidays. For a general overview of our benefits, please visit our careers page at https://miller-remick.com/career-page/.

We are an equal opportunity employer. We provide reasonable accommodations in accordance with applicable law.

new_jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent Work Model:
Remote Reference code:
135595 Primary Location:
Toronto, ON All Available Locations:
Toronto, ON; Halifax, NS; Ottawa, ON

Our Purpose

At Deloitte, our Purpose is to make an impact that matters. We exist to inspire and help our people, organizations, communities, and countries to thrive by building a better future. Our work underpins a prosperous society where people can find meaning and opportunity. It builds consumer and business confidence, empowers organizations to find imaginative ways of deploying capital, enables fair, trusted, and functioning social and economic institutions, and allows our friends, families, and communities to enjoy the quality of life that comes with a sustainable future. And as the largest 100% Canadian-owned and operated professional services firm in our country, we are proud to work alongside our clients to make a positive impact for all Canadians.

By living our Purpose, we will make an impact that matters.

Have many careers in one Firm.
Enjoy flexible, proactive, and practical benefits that foster a culture of well-being and connectedness.
Learn from deep subject matter experts through mentoring and on the job coaching

Deloitte Global is the engine of the Deloitte network. Our professionals reach across disciplines and borders to develop and lead global initiatives. We deliver strategic programs and services that unite our organization.

What will your typical day look like?

Global Talent Operations (GTO) is responsible for operating and delivering globally provided talent technology platforms & tools, content, and services to enable Deloitte’s talent strategy across the network.

Within GTO, the Digital and Data Enablement team enables the successful delivery of strategic global talent technology projects; shepherding the priority from strategy to technology implementation, adoption and ultimate transition to BAU operations. Digital and Data Enablement works across GTO service offerings and specializes in understanding how technology, operations and talent priorities intersect – regardless of the domain.

As a Project Manager, you will work directly with GTO service offering teams, delivery partners (e.g., Deloitte Technology, external vendors), and stakeholders (e.g., Global Talent, member firm, global business) serving as a product owner of new or decommissioning services, products or priorities.

Responsibilities:

Drive cross-functional teams in the delivery of complex projects with global impact; combine analytical thinking, operational excellence, and program management to help move initiatives from concept and strategy to practical execution.
Act as a bridge between technical teams, vendors, member firms, and the internal leadership group to create alignment and drive structured decision-making.
Develop and demonstrate strong business knowledge of assigned projects; translate business requirements into strategies that support operational needs and long-term transformation goals.
Lead and manage a diverse range of talent technology projects including system implementations, major updates, system decommissioning, and data/reporting projects to enable global talent strategy while ensuring timely delivery and high-quality outcomes.
Lead project issue/risk management, remediation plans, and escalations across teams for projects - responsible for providing management direction in these areas and ensuring clear communication, consideration of all factors, generation of solution alternatives, and defined actionable plans.
Build detailed project master schedules and promote collaboration through identified team sites.
Prepare and deliver regular, audience-specific communications, presentations, and reports/dashboards to ensure that program sponsors, key stakeholders, and leadership are adequately apprised of complex program and project statuses, successes, risks and issues.
Motivate and lead project teams and fosters a mindset of collaboration and continuous process improvement.

About The Team

Global CoRe is a shared service within Deloitte Global, providing fundamental services to Deloitte People around the world: Knowledge Services, Creative Services, Contact Center, Procurement and Strategic Insights Center. We deliver essential capabilities that save time, convey insights, minimize risk, enhance client service delivery, solve problems, and contribute to Deloitte’s success.

Enough About Us, Let’s Talk About You

Required Qualifications:

5+ years of relevant experience working on large, complex, cross-functional initiatives and/or enterprise talent platforms
3+ years of experience in product management owning and driving product roadmap, backlog and delivery of releases
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Business Administration, Learning Technology, Human Resources, or equivalent educational or professional experience
Strong communication, presentation, stakeholder management, and relationship-building skills in a global, virtual, cross-functional environment

Other Qualifications:

Ability to balance strategic thinking with practical delivery, stakeholder alignment, and comfort working through ambiguity and competing priorities.
Understanding of both technology and operational processes, and ability to connect dots between those processes and business needs.
Strong analytical mindset with the ability to translate data, user feedback, platform trends, and stakeholder needs into actionable recommendations.
Demonstrated ability to influence without authority and drive alignment across technology, business, vendor, and operations teams.
Commitment to delivering a seamless, inclusive, and engaging stakeholder experience across global audiences.

Total Rewards

The salary range for this position is $85,000 - $156,000, and individuals may be eligible to participate in our bonus program. Deloitte is fair and competitive when it comes to the salaries of our people. We regularly benchmark across a variety of positions, industries, sectors, targets, and levels. Our approach is grounded on recognizing people's unique strengths and contributions and rewarding the value that they deliver.

Our Total Rewards Package extends well beyond traditional compensation and benefit programs and is designed to recognize employee contributions, encourage personal wellness, and support firm growth. Along with a competitive base salary and variable pay opportunities, we offer a wide array of initiatives that differentiate us as a people-first organization. On top of our regular paid vacation days, some examples include: $4,000 per year for mental health support benefits, a $1,300 flexible benefit spending account, firm-wide closures known as "Deloitte Days", dedicated days of for learning (known as Development and Innovation Days), flexible work arrangements and a hybrid work structure.

Our promise to our people: Deloitte is where potential comes to life.

Be yourself, and more.

We are a group of talented people who want to learn, gain experience, and develop skills. Wherever you are in your career, we want you to advance.

You Shape How We Make Impact.

Diverse perspectives and life experiences make us better. Whoever you are and wherever you’re from, we want you to feel like you belong here. We provide flexible working options to support you and how you can contribute.

Be the leader you want to be

Some guide teams, some change culture, some build essential expertise. We offer opportunities and experiences that support your continuing growth as a leader.

Have as many careers as you want.

We are uniquely able to offer you new challenges and roles – and prepare you for them. We bring together people with unique experiences and talents, and we are the place to develop a lasting network of friends, peers, and mentors.

The next step is yours

At Deloitte, we are all about doing business inclusively – that starts with having diverse colleagues of all abilities. Deloitte encourages applications from all qualified candidates who represent the full diversity of communities across Canada. This includes, but is not limited to, people with disabilities, candidates from Indigenous communities, and candidates from the Black community in support of living our values, creating a culture of Diversity Equity and Inclusion and our commitment to our AccessAbility Action Plan, Reconciliation Action Plan and the BlackNorth Initiative.

We encourage you to connect with us at accessiblecareers@deloitte.ca if you require an accommodation for the recruitment process (including alternate formats of materials, accessible meeting rooms or other accommodations) or indigenouscareers@deloitte.ca for any questions relating to careers for Indigenous peoples at Deloitte (First Nations, Inuit, Métis).

When you apply, we will review your application using Deloitte's Global Talent Standards to ensure a consistent recruitment experience. Our recruitment advisors and hiring teams will utilize human screening combined with AI technology to help identify the skills and qualities that matter most to our business, while safeguarding your privacy and using AI responsibly.

Deloitte Canada has 20 offices with representation across most of the country. We acknowledge that Deloitte offices stand on traditional, treaty, and unceded territories in what is now known as Canada. We recognize that Indigenous Peoples have been the caretakers of this land since time immemorial, nurturing its resources and preserving its natural beauty. We acknowledge this land is still home to many First Nations, Inuit, and Métis Peoples, who continue to maintain their deep connection to the land and its sacred teachings. We humbly acknowledge that we are all Treaty people, and we commit to fostering a relationship of respect, collaboration, and stewardship with Indigenous communities in our shared goal of reconciliation and environmental sustainability.

new_jobs.title: Data Center COE Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
At ABB
, we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. You’ll be empowered to lead, supported to grow, and proud of the impact we create together. Join us and help run what runs the world.

This position reports to:

Service Project Management Manager

__

In this role, you lead the end‑to‑end execution of Start‑up, Commissioning, and aftermarket service projects within the Data Center Services Center of Excellence. The portfolio includes Paralleling Switchgear and Protection & Control projects across the U.S. Electrification Service business. You set clear guidelines, define tasks and milestones, and drive performance through strong coordination, motivation, and feedback. You also safeguard and elevate customer satisfaction by ensuring all requirements, commitments, and project targets are consistently met, delivering high‑quality service at every stage of the engagement.

The work model for the role is: Remote in the US

This role is contributing to the Electrification Services Business Area
in the United States.

In this role your main accountabilities are:

Leads the project team by establishing execution approach and overseeing project hand-over, planning, monitoring and control activities for internal and external resources and accomplishing project goals
Managing the development of project planning documents
Monitoring projects to ensure best practices in cost control, resource efficiency and Health, Safety & Environment (HSE)
Analyzing and addressing project risks, and regularly disseminating lessons learned
Working with other functions to coordinate contract negotiations and claims with customers
Managing external suppliers to ensure availability of equipment, systems, material and services
Serve as an escalation point for project issues.
Achieving project deliverables and compliance with contract requirements
Building strong relationships with customers and stakeholders

Qualifications for the role:

A Bachelor of Science degree in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering highly preferred. Combination of education and relevant experience will be considered in lieu of.
3+ years of experience in the electrical industry working as a subject matter expert or project manager with paralleling switchgear, protection and control systems, electrical energy management systems, or electrical field services in the data center or power generation/distribution market

Job Description

This role oversees the technical design and delivery of drinking water and wastewater projects, from conceptual design through construction documentation. The Civil Project Manager leads feasibility studies, hydraulic and process modeling, and treatment process design while coordinating closely with project teams and municipal and utility clients. The position offers a direct placement opportunity with potential for contract-to-hire and supports a growing portfolio of water and wastewater infrastructure projects across multiple regions.

Responsibilities

Assist with leading the technical design and delivery of drinking water and wastewater projects, including permitting, hydraulic modeling, treatment process design, pump stations, pipelines, OA/SCADA integrations, GUDI considerations, headworks, disinfection, residuals management, and nutrient removal as applicable.
Conceptualize the initial design approach for major phases of large projects, ensuring alignment with project objectives and regulatory requirements.
Lead and participate in feasibility studies, alternatives analyses, and screening-level designs to evaluate technical solutions and support decision-making.
Perform sizing, hydraulic modeling, contaminant analyses, and compliance analyses to support design development and regulatory approvals.
Participate in the preparation of construction drawings, high-level engineering calculations or models, technical specifications, and cost estimates for drinking water and wastewater projects.
Provide project-specific technical information and guidance to design staff and project managers for incorporation into project specifications and construction drawings.
Coordinate with multidisciplinary teams to ensure that designs for drinking water, sanitary sewer, and water treatment facilities are accurate, constructible, and aligned with client needs.
Support all aspects of project development, including design, construction coordination, environmental design considerations, budgeting, and administrative project tasks.
Collaborate with municipalities and utility companies to support the design and development of drinking water and wastewater facilities.
Utilize design and modeling tools such as AutoCAD Civil 3D, WaterCAD, WaterGEMS, SewerCAD, or similar software to develop and refine project designs.

Essential Skills

At least 4+ years of experience in drinking water and/or wastewater engineering, including design, construction, and environmental design.
Experience managing all aspects of project development, including budgeting and administrative issues related to project delivery.
Strong understanding of drinking water treatment and wastewater treatment processes.
Proficiency with hydraulic and process modeling software such as WaterCAD, WaterGEMS, SewerCAD, or similar tools.
Experience with design software including AutoCAD, Civil 3D, and GIS.
Technical background in drinking water, sanitary sewer, and water treatment systems.
Ability to perform hydraulic modeling, contaminant analyses, and compliance analyses to support design and regulatory submissions.
Solid foundation in civil engineering principles related to water and wastewater infrastructure.
Capability to prepare construction drawings, engineering calculations, technical specifications, and cost estimates.

Position Summary

Are you an experienced project professional who enjoys taking ownership of complex engineered equipment projects and working directly with customers, engineers, manufacturing teams, and suppliers?

TIC is seeking a Motor Project Manager to lead customer projects involving medium-voltage electric motors from order acceptance through final delivery and customer acceptance.

In this highly visible role, you will serve as the primary point of contact for assigned projects, coordinating activities across engineering, manufacturing, sales, logistics, suppliers, and customers. You will manage project schedules, budgets, documentation, technical requirements, and customer expectations while helping ensure each project is delivered safely, accurately, on time, and in accordance with contractual commitments.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who combines technical knowledge, customer service, and project leadership and wants to play a key role in bringing large, engineered motor projects from order to successful completion.

What You’ll Do

Project Leadership & Execution

Manage assigned medium-voltage motor projects from order acceptance through shipment, commissioning support, and final customer acceptance.
Serve as the primary point of contact for customers throughout the project lifecycle.
Develop and maintain project schedules, milestones, deliverables, and customer commitments.
Coordinate cross-functional activities involving Sales, Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Logistics, and other internal and external partners.
Identify project risks, schedule concerns, technical issues, and potential roadblocks and work with the appropriate teams to drive timely resolution.
Monitor project progress and provide regular status updates to customers and internal stakeholders.

Build strong, professional relationships with customers, suppliers, and project stakeholders.
Act as a customer advocate while balancing contractual requirements, business objectives, schedules, and project costs.
Coordinate and participate in customer meetings, project reviews, and site visits as needed.
Support and host customer-witnessed testing at TIC or partner manufacturing facilities.
Communicate project changes, risks, delays, and resolutions clearly and proactively.

Review customer purchase orders, specifications, and project documentation to ensure alignment with TIC commitments.
Manage project costs and authorized expenditures while supporting established budget and margin objectives.
Coordinate project requirements related to invoicing, progress payments, and title transfers in accordance with applicable JSOX requirements.
Monitor commercial and contractual obligations throughout the life of the project.

Technical Coordination

Review and interpret engineering drawings, schematics, specifications, customer documentation, and project requirements.
Coordinate technical questions and documentation between customers and internal engineering teams.
Support the resolution of technical and manufacturing issues that could affect project schedule, cost, quality, or customer requirements.
Apply working knowledge of medium-voltage motors and applicable industry standards throughout project execution.

What You’ll Bring

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, Project Management, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience.
2 to 8 years of relevant industry experience, including experience supporting or managing engineered equipment projects.
Working knowledge of medium-voltage motors or comparable large industrial rotating equipment.
Ability to read and understand technical drawings, specifications, and engineering documentation.
Strong project organization, prioritization, and problem-solving skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively across technical, manufacturing, commercial, and customer-facing teams.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and stakeholders in a project-driven environment.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and standard business/project management systems.
Ability to travel approximately 5% to 10%, including occasional visits to customer sites, manufacturing facilities, or supplier locations.

Preferred Qualifications

Direct experience managing medium-voltage motor projects.
Knowledge of applicable motor industry standards, including:
API 541
API 547
IEEE 841

Familiarity with Incoterms and international or domestic equipment shipments.
Experience working with engineered-to-order or configure-to-order industrial equipment.
Experience coordinating customer-witnessed testing or factory acceptance testing.
Familiarity with ERP, CRM, and project scheduling tools such as Microsoft Project.
Experience working in an industrial manufacturing or heavy-equipment environment.

What Success Looks Like

A successful Motor Project Manager will:

Take ownership of projects and drive them forward from order through final acceptance.
Develop trusted relationships with customers and internal stakeholders.
Anticipate project risks rather than simply reacting to problems.
Keep engineering, manufacturing, logistics, sales, and customers aligned on priorities and commitments.
Communicate clearly when project requirements, schedules, or circumstances change.
Balance customer satisfaction, technical requirements, schedule, cost, quality, and business objectives.
Remain organized and effective while managing multiple active projects and competing priorities.

Tools & Technology

Experience With Or The Ability To Quickly Learn

Microsoft Office
Microsoft Outlook
Microsoft Project
ERP systems
CRM systems
Windows-based business applications

Approximately 5% to 10%, depending on project and customer requirements.

Travel may include customer sites, TIC facilities, supplier locations, and manufacturing facilities.

This position primarily operates in a professional office environment but may also involve visits to manufacturing facilities, customer sites, and supplier locations.

Stand or walk for extended periods
Climb, stoop, squat, or bend
Lift, carry, push, or pull up to 20 pounds

Approximately 75% of work is performed in a temperature-controlled environment.

Approximately 25% may be performed in a manufacturing plant, field environment, customer location, or supplier facility. These environments may include exposure to high voltage, industrial equipment, elevated noise levels, changing weather conditions, and other typical industrial hazards.
