new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Tiered Approach

In Line With The Commitment To Safeguard Capacity And Support Personnel Already In The Organization, a Majority Of UNDP UNCDF/UNV Vacancies Are Advertised Using a Tiered Application Process Whereby

Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.
Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments
Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers
Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

In 2025, the National Council of Justice (CNJ) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) established a partnership aimed at promoting innovation in cybersecurity for the Brazilian Judiciary. Project BRA/25/025 develops and implements tools and strategies to strengthen cybersecurity, digital preservation and information integrity, expanding the protection of the Judiciary’s systems and users.

The initiative strengthens institutional security and promotes transparency, good governance and the efficiency of judicial processes, contributing to resource savings and to a more agile Justice system for the benefit of citizens and society.

To this end, the project governance is organized into the following fronts:

Four Cross-cutting Coordination Axes

General Coordination;
Integrated Monitoring and Control Unit;
Technical and Operational Management Unit;
Training and Communication Unit;

Four Workstreams, Focused On

Regulatory compliance;
Operational conformity;
Network governance;
Promotion of a cybersecurity culture;

As this is a home-based position, the candidate is expected to have adequate working conditions, including the infrastructure and equipment necessary for the full performance of the activities.

Duties And Responsibilities

The Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst will be assigned to the Network Governance axis and will be responsible for leading the collection, analysis and dissemination of cyber threat intelligence, with the aim of anticipating risks, enriching the understanding of incidents and threat actors, and strengthening the resilience of Judiciary institutions within the context of project BRA/25/025.

The incumbent will work in close coordination with the CNJ and UNDP teams, and the following indicative activities are foreseen:

Cyber Intelligence Coordination and Dissemination

Engage in the threat information-sharing network among Judiciary bodies, ensuring the smooth flow of tactical and operational data.
Produce intelligence inputs for operational alerts, threat advisories, and rapid dissemination bulletins for technical teams and managers.
Facilitate cooperation with national and international Computer Security Incident Response Teams (CSIRTs) and public sector cooperation networks.
Contribute to a proactive, forward-looking cyber defense posture for the Judiciary, anticipating threats based on the intelligence produced and shared.
Support the operation and curation of intelligence-sharing platforms (e.g., MISP, OpenCTI), using standards such as STIX/TAXII and the Traffic Light Protocol (TLP) for the classification and dissemination of information.

Intelligence Production and Threat Analysis

Conduct advanced analyses of threat actors, their motivations, capabilities and TTPs (Tactics, Techniques and Procedures), applying analytical models such as the Diamond Model and the Cyber Kill Chain.
Transform raw data from technical, open and internal sources into actionable intelligence to support proactive defense and improve incident containment, observing operational security (OPSEC) best practices in collection activities.
Support vulnerability prioritization based on the actual likelihood of exploitation in the current threat landscape.
Monitor open sources, forums, deep and dark web channels, and national and international technical reports to identify campaigns, data leaks and threats targeting the public sector and the Judiciary.
Define, maintain and periodically review Priority Intelligence Requirements (PIRs), ensuring intelligence production remains aligned with organizational risks, priorities and the evolving threat landscape.

Strengthening Proactive Detection

Produce and provide indicators of compromise (IoCs), behavioral patterns and detection signatures/rules (e.g., YARA, Sigma, Snort/Suricata) to feed monitoring systems (SIEM, EDR, IDS/IPS, etc.).
Collaborate with Blue Team, Threat Hunting and Incident Response teams to validate intrusion hypotheses based on threat intelligence.
Assess the effectiveness of security coverage against techniques mapped in frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK, identifying detection gaps and proposing adjustments.
Support the automation and orchestration of intelligence workflows (collection, enrichment, correlation and distribution), integrating CTI platforms with SOAR and monitoring tools.
Support the analysis of incident-related artifacts, logs and relevant technical evidence to extract relevant IoCs and TTPs.

Strategic Risk Management and Security Posture

Contribute to periodic security posture reviews with an external view of threats specifically targeting the public sector and the Judiciary.
Identify long-term cyberattack trends to guide investments and changes in the defense architecture.
Propose improvements to technical controls based on the evolution of identified threats.
Support External Attack Surface Management (EASM) activities by identifying exposed assets, leaked credentials and indicators of organizational exposure.

Integration with Capacity Building and Innovation

Integrate real-world threat intelligence into Situational Awareness programs to raise user maturity against targeted attacks.
Promote the use of CTI frameworks (e.g., MITRE ATT&CK, Diamond Model, Cyber Kill Chain), OPSEC best practices and security data analysis.

Continuity, Reporting and Simulations

Participate in the development of realistic threat scenarios for crisis simulation exercises and continuity plans.
Produce technical intelligence reports, threat assessments, and executive summaries tailored to technical teams and senior management.
Conduct workshops and training on intelligence analysis for local teams.

Knowledge Management

Document analysis methodologies and lessons learned from relevant incidents, and keep the knowledge base on sector adversaries up to date.
Develop and maintain analytical templates, reporting standards and intelligence production guidelines to ensure consistency across the intelligence lifecycle.
Promote the reuse of intelligence products across Incident Response, Threat Hunting, Vulnerability Management and Security Operations teams

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Project.

Institutional Arrangement

The incumbent will be supervised by the Governance and Network Management Analyst.

Competencies

Core competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Direction & Strategy | Strategic Thinking:

Develop effective strategies and prioritized plans in line with UNDP’s objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, potential risks and opportunities; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight

Business Direction & Strategy | Business Acumen:

Ability to understand and deal with a business situation in a manner that is likely to lead to a good outcome. Ability to make good judgments and quick decisions within such frameworks in the organization. Knowledge and understanding of the operational frameworks in the organization.

Business Development | Human-centered Design:

Ability to develop solutions to problems by involving the human perspective in all steps of the problem-solving process. Knowledge and understanding of human-centered design principles and practices.

Business Management | Project Management:

Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management.

Digital | Cyber and Data Privacy Security Risk Management:

Ability to anticipate, prepare for and respond to potential Risks and issues that may results in Data breaches that can cause potential identity theft and personal harm and can also negatively impact UNDP's reputation

2030 Agenda: Peace | Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights:

Effective Justice Sector Institutions

2030 Agenda: Peace | Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights:

Access to Justice

Required Skills And Experience

Min. Education requirements:

Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in Information Security, Information Technology, Information Systems, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Telecommunications Engineering, Electrical Engineering or related fields is required, or
A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Min. Years Of Relevant Work Experience

Applicants with Master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience.
Applicants with a Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of two (2) years of experience in Cyber Threat Intelligence.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section:

Recognized complementary training in CTI, OSINT, OPSEC, digital forensics or related areas.
Previous experience in a Security Operations Center (SOC), CSIRT/CERT or dedicated threat intelligence team, preferably in the public sector or the justice system.
Experience in collecting and analyzing open-source intelligence and in using cyber threat intelligence platforms (e.g., MISP, OpenCTI).
Experience using scripting and query languages (e.g., Python, KQL, SPL) for collecting, parsing and analyzing large volumes of security data.
Experience in writing technical and executive reports on cyber threats.
Experience with the Brazilian legal and regulatory framework on cybersecurity and data protection.

Required Language(s)

Fluency in Portuguese is required.
Fluency in English is desirable.

Professional Certificates

N/A

GreenShield is a proudly Canadian, national non-profit health care and insurance organization, driven by our mission of Better Health for All. We believe health care is a right, not a privilege, and we are committed to improving health outcomes, advancing health equity, and building a future where every Canadian can reach their full health and well-being potential. Through our unique integrated payer-provider ("payvider") model, we offer insurance, administer benefits, and pay claims as a ‘payer’ while offering health care services such as mental health, pharmacy, telemedicine, and chronic disease management as a ‘provider’. As a non-profit social enterprise without shareholders, we reinvest our excess earnings to directly support underserved communities. Through GreenShield Cares, we positively impacted the health and well-being of over one million Canadians between 2020 and 2025. What’s driving us now is the commitment to measurably impact an additional three million Canadians by 2030 – across mental health, essential medicines, and chronic disease management – through scalable initiatives that deliver meaningful change in pursuit of our mission of Better Health for All. At GreenShield, our culture is where purpose meets passion and performance. Our teams work as one to deliver meaningful, measurable impact for the people and communities we serve.

THE ROLE IN A NUTSHELL

The Business Intelligence Analyst enables data‑driven decision‑making by delivering high‑quality, actionable insights aligned to organizational priorities. Acting as a bridge between business stakeholders and technical teams, the role ensures analytics solutions are scalable, accurate, and governed by enterprise data standards. Through proactive performance monitoring and analysis, the Analyst supports strategic and operational improvement across the organization.
Responsibilities include:
Design, develop, and maintain business intelligence reports, dashboards, and metrics aligned with strategic and operational goals.
Translate business requirements into technical specifications and partner with data and analytics teams to deliver effective BI solutions.
Ensure data integrity, governance, and consistency by adhering to enterprise data standards and architecture.
Monitor key performance indicators to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for continuous improvement.
Conduct ad‑hoc and deep‑dive analyses to support leadership decision‑making and business initiatives.
Present insights and recommendations clearly to both technical and non‑technical audiences.
Support and enable business users through guidance on BI tools, data interpretation, and best practices.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Post‑secondary degree in computer science, data science, mathematics, statistics, or a related field.
3+ years of hands‑on experience designing and delivering BI reports, dashboards, and scorecards using tools such as Power BI, Tableau, or Looker.
Strong technical proficiency in data querying, transformation, and modeling using SQL and related languages (e.g., DAX, Power Query, M).
Experience developing end‑to‑end BI solutions, including ETL processes, relational databases, data warehouses, and cloud data platforms (e.g., Azure Synapse, Snowflake, BigQuery).
Proven ability to work with large, complex datasets and translate business requirements into scalable, actionable insights while ensuring data quality and governance.
Strong communication, storytelling, and collaboration skills, with experience engaging both technical and non‑technical stakeholders.

NICE TO HAVE

Knowledge of scripting languages (e.g., Python, R) for advanced analytics or automation.
Exposure to machine learning or predictive analytics concepts and their integration into BI workflows.
Background in training or mentoring business users on BI tools and data literacy.
Bilingual in French and English.

THE CULTURE

We believe a career should be meaningful. Not just a means to earn a living. Our culture is one where everyone's voice is heard and valued. Because that’s what it takes to create better health for all. We dare to challenge the status quo. And we’re driven by people who have challenged theirs. We believe that your workplace should empower you to be the best version of yourself. That’s why we provide a place where you can be inspired, challenged, and rewarded.

The role

As a Senior Security Analyst, you'll lead the response to complex cyber security threats, acting as the highest technical escalation point within our SOC. You'll investigate and contain incidents, hunt for emerging threats, enhance detection capabilities, and help strengthen customer security across SIEM, SOAR, EDR/XDR, cloud and identity platforms. You'll also contribute to automation, playbook development, service improvements and the growth of the wider SOC team, while participating in an on-call rota with additional allowances and overtime where applicable.

What will I be doing?

Security Monitoring & Incident Response

Lead major incident investigations, response and customer communications.
Analyse and remediate threats across SIEM, EDR/XDR, cloud and identity platforms.
Produce incident reports, root cause analysis and response recommendations.

Threat Hunting & Intelligence

Proactively hunt for threats and investigate emerging attack techniques.
Leverage threat intelligence to improve detection and response capabilities.
Enhance coverage aligned to the MITRE ATT&CK framework.

Detection Engineering & Automation

Develop and optimise detections, analytics and SOAR playbooks.
Improve alert quality, monitoring visibility and response automation.
Support onboarding of new security tools and log sources.

Technical Leadership

Act as the senior escalation point for SOC analysts.
Mentor junior team members and uphold investigation quality.
Contribute to training, documentation and continuous improvement.

Customer Engagement

Provide technical expertise during customer incidents and reviews.
Deliver security findings, recommendations and service guidance.
Support customer onboarding and ongoing security optimisation.

Operational Excellence

Maintain compliance with SLAs, processes and documentation standards.
Support audits, service development and continuous improvement initiatives.

What will I bring to the role?

Technical Knowledge

Strong knowledge of modern security operations, threat detection and incident response.
Experience with SIEM, SOAR, EDR/XDR, cloud and identity security platforms.
Understanding of threat intelligence, threat hunting, MITRE ATT&CK and detection engineering.
Familiarity with Windows, networking, cloud security, vulnerability management and KQL.

Experience

Experience within a SOC, MDR, MSSP or cyber security operations environment.
Proven ability to investigate high-severity security incidents.
Hands-on experience with SIEM, EDR and customer-facing incident response.
Comfortable producing technical reports and mentoring junior analysts.

Desirable Technical Skills

PowerShell and Python scripting.
API integrations and security automation.
Detection engineering and content development.
SOAR playbook creation and optimisation.

new_jobs.title: Research Operations Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

We are seeking a Research Operations Analyst
to support a multi-year mineral title consolidation program for one of the largest royalty funds in the United States.

This is a program-scale, long-term engagement
that spans the full retitling pipeline- from title research through revenue recovery
. The role begins with a strong focus on chain-of-title research
, but is designed as an entry point into a broader operational career path across adjacent functions including curative resolution, owner communications, recording operations, and revenue administration
.

The ideal candidate combines the analytical rigor of a legal researcher
, the precision of a data analyst
, and the operational adaptability
to learn and execute across evolving workflows.

Key Responsibilities

Conduct structured chain-of-title research for owner/fund pairs, tracing ownership histories from current ownership back to origin.
Review and interpret legal documents including deeds, probate filings, court orders, affidavits, conveyance instruments, and powers of attorney.
Cross-reference ownership data across multiple sources (county records, ownership registers, transfer histories) to verify accuracy and identify discrepancies.
Identify and document title gaps, ownership defects, missing documents, inflated decimals, and chain breaks, and flag issues for review and resolution.
Classify ownership records using the program's A/B classification framework (clean title vs. curative required).
Enter research findings into structured databases using defined workflows and validation protocols.
Assemble and maintain complete evidence packs, including supporting documents, source references, and classification rationale, with proper version control.
Ensure all research outputs meet quality standards, targeting a 90%+ first-pass acceptance rate, and participate in quality control audits.
Navigate and extract data from county clerk and recorder systems across multiple jurisdictions, adapting to varying formats and access methods.
Use land records aggregator platforms where direct county access is limited or incomplete, and document county-specific access constraints.
Maintain consistent productivity against defined throughput benchmarks, with improving efficiency over time.
Follow established research methodologies, SOPs, and workflow protocols, and incorporate feedback to continuously improve accuracy.
Cross-train into additional operational functions over time, including curative resolution, owner communications, recording operations, operator engagement, and revenue transition workflows, following structured training and competency assessments.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Law, Business, Finance, Political Science, Public Administration, or a related field.
Strong analytical and research skills with exceptional attention to detail and ability to maintain accuracy across high-volume work.
Ability to read, interpret, and extract information from legal and property-related documents.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook) and comfort working with structured databases.
Strong written communication skills to document findings, flag issues, and assemble structured evidence files.
Ability to manage multiple workflows simultaneously while maintaining organization and meeting productivity targets.
Self-disciplined, reliable, and comfortable working within structured processes and defined methodologies.
Strong learning agility and adaptability as responsibilities expand across the operational pipeline.
Fluency in English is required; French, Arabic, or Urdu is a plus.

Nice to Have

Experience in title research, legal research, land records, real estate transactions, or property administration.
Familiarity with U.S. county records systems, land data platforms, or document aggregator services.
Understanding of property ownership structures, mineral rights, or chain-of-title concepts.
Experience in data entry, document review, or compliance-driven environments with quality standards.
Exposure to oil & gas operations, royalty administration, or mineral interest management.
Experience working in cross-functional, distributed teams across multiple time zones.

Artificial Intelligence & Automation

Operations Business Analyst

Are you someone who can look at business performance, spot what others may be missing, and use data to uncover what is driving the results?

The Operations Business Analyst reports to Recovery Operations and serves as a shared analytical resource across Recovery Operations, Operational Excellence, and Finance. You will build and maintain operational dashboards that make business performance visible, but the role goes well beyond reporting. You will investigate what the data is telling us, determine why performance is changing, identify where processes or results are breaking down, and provide clear, actionable insights that help business leaders determine where action is needed.

The ideal candidate combines strong business judgment with hands-on analytical capability. You can build a Power BI dashboard, but more importantly, you know what to look for, what questions to ask, and how to turn what you find into meaningful business insight.

What You'll Do

Identify Performance Issues & Opportunities

Analyze productivity, inventory quality, throughput, recovery performance, capacity, cycle time, and financial results.
Conduct root-cause analysis to understand why performance is improving, declining, or deviating from expectations.
Identify issues that may require operational, process, workflow, or technology changes.
Translate findings into clear, actionable insights for business leaders.

Build Performance Visibility

Develop and maintain Power BI dashboards and reports that provide meaningful visibility into business performance.

Measure Business Impact

Evaluate the impact of workflow changes, process improvements, and automation initiatives.
Determine whether implemented changes are producing the intended operational and financial results.
Develop scenario analyses, forecasts, and performance projections to support business decisions.
Identify new risks, opportunities, or performance issues revealed by changing results

Partner Across the Business

Provide the analysis and insights needed to help leaders prioritize where action is required.

new_jobs.title: Policy Program Manager, Safeguards Regulatory
new_jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

As a Program Manager on Anthropic's Safeguards team, you'll help make sure we meet our obligations under AI safety laws and regulations around the world. Working closely with Legal, you'll turn new and emerging requirements into programs, controls, and deliverables. This requires a detailed understanding of how our models and products are built, evaluated and safeguarded. Your work will support Anthropic's commitment to developing AI safely and beneficially as the regulatory landscape evolves.

The responsibilities listed below are some examples of areas that someone in this role could own, depending on their experience and the team's needs.

Key Responsibilities

Manage and drive complex safety initiatives that identify, assess and mitigate risks from frontier models, from initial risk assessment through to the deployment of safeguards
Partner with the Safeguards incident management team to strengthen incident response and reporting processes, including the policies that determine how incidents are escalated and when they must be reported externally
Conduct post-incident reviews, and work with the subject matter experts for each harm area to incorporate the findings into model and product safeguards
Own the safety strategy and deliverables for AI systems used in high-risk settings, including risk assessments, technical documentation, and the information that deploying customers need to use those systems safely
Define the safety and risk controls that our models and products require, ensure that each control has an owner and a documented procedure, and confirm that it operates as intended
Partner closely with the owners of each risk area to develop a deep understanding of AI risks, safety evaluations and mitigation strategies, and use that understanding to prepare safety documentation, transparency reports and regulatory submissions

Minimum Qualifications

Experience in trust and safety, AI safety or a related field, including designing and implementing safeguards against misuse or harm
Understanding of AI safety, including the principal risk areas and the evaluations and safeguards used to address them, well enough to engage substantively with the technical experts responsible for them
Experience running risk assessment or harm mitigation programs from identification through to resolution
Experience translating policy or regulatory requirements into practical operational processes
Ability to drive complex, cross-functional programs to completion in a fast-moving environment, including with technical teams outside your own discipline
Clear written communication, including documentation for technical, legal and external audiences
Strong attention to detail, and the judgment to recognize when work is at risk and raise it early
Commitment to the safe development and deployment of AI

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with AI-specific regulation, such as the EU AI Act
Experience leading incident response programs, including escalation paths and external reporting obligations
Experience preparing safety documentation, transparency reports or regulatory submissions
Experience working with technical and research teams on safety evaluations

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary

$245,000—$285,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

new_jobs.title: Senior Business Operations Analyst
new_jobs.description:
The Business Operations team sits within Finance and partners across Chainalysis to strengthen how the company plans, makes decisions, and executes. Combining analytical rigor with practical operating judgment, the team helps leaders translate company priorities into clear plans, effective operating rhythms, and measurable outcomes. As Chainalysis continues to evolve, Business Operations also helps build the processes and ways of working that enable teams to scale and adapt.

You’ll join a close-knit team working with partners across Finance, R&D, go-to-market, Legal, Security, and beyond. The team takes on high-priority work across the business, often creating structure where approaches are still taking shape, and helps teams align and move change forward. This role offers broad exposure to Chainalysis and the opportunity to help shape how the company operates through its next stage of growth.

In this role, you’ll:

As a Senior Business Operations Analyst at Chainalysis, you will be a strategic operator and connective tissue across leadership and functions - helping translate company priorities into clear plans, operating rhythms, and measurable outcomes. You’ll partner with leaders across Finance, Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and other teams to improve how the business plans, makes decisions, and executes.

You’ll support high-priority, cross-functional initiatives end to end: framing ambiguous problems, developing analyses and recommendations, aligning stakeholders, establishing milestones and governance, and driving follow-through. You’ll help run planning and business review cadences, build KPI reporting and insights, improve processes and systems, and support change initiatives such as pricing and packaging, go-to-market readiness, product launches, and organizational or operating-model changes.

You will also:

Identify friction in cross-functional workflows and design scalable processes, tools, and operating mechanisms.
Prepare clear, data-informed recommendations and executive-ready materials.
Manage multiple work-streams and facilitate alignment across stakeholders, balancing speed, rigor, and effective change management.

We are looking for candidates who have/are:

3–6 years of experience in business operations, strategy and operations, management consulting, finance, program management, or a related field—ideally in a SaaS or technology environment.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate data into insights, recommendations, and decisions.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to create executive-ready narratives and materials.
Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives from problem definition through implementation and measurable outcomes.
Strong project and program management skills, including prioritization, stakeholder management, and attention to detail.
Familiarity with business intelligence, data, and collaboration tools; experience with Jira, Confluence, Databricks, spreadsheets, SQL, and/or AI-powered tools is a plus.
Ability to drive clarity in ambiguity, influence without authority, and demonstrate resilience in a dynamic environment.
Curious, adaptable, and motivated to learn quickly, challenge assumptions, and make the company and team better.

Nice to have experience:

Business Operations or Strategy & Operations experience in a high-growth SaaS or technology company.
Supporting annual or quarterly planning, operating cadences, business reviews, resource allocation, or strategic planning processes.
Establishing KPIs, building performance dashboards, and using data to identify trends, risks, and opportunities.
Supporting pricing and packaging, go-to-market or commercialization initiatives, product launches, or broader change-management efforts.
Applying agile, lean, or other process-improvement methodologies to scale how teams work.
Interest in and general knowledge of blockchain and cryptocurrency, including key players and market dynamics.

AI at Chainalysis

AI is not a feature at Chainalysis - it is a new way of working. One that turns instructions into work done, and helps us move faster than the threats we're built to counter, and we expect our employees to take ownership of the output and ensure quality. As the world's most trusted blockchain analytics platform, Chainalysis sits at a rare intersection of proprietary data, regulatory relationships and crypto expertise that makes it uniquely placed to shape and lead the next era of AI-driven intelligence - and we expect everyone here, regardless of role, to be an active part of it.

AI fluency is tied directly to how we measure performance and how we plan to win. There is no substitute for your own curiosity. We provide the tools, workflows, and space to experiment - but the expectation is that you develop these capabilities yourself, bring ideas, and collaborate across teams to reinvent the way work gets done. We are not using AI to do less. We are using it to do what was never possible before.

About Chainalysis

Chainalysis is the blockchain data platform, making it easy to connect the movement of digital assets to real-world services. Powered by deep blockchain data and AI, organizations can investigate illicit activity, manage risk exposure, and develop innovative market solutions built on the industry's most trusted blockchain intelligence. Our mission is to build trust in blockchains, blending safety and security with an unwavering commitment to growth and innovation.

You belong here.

At Chainalysis, we believe that diversity of experience and thought makes us stronger. With both customers and employees around the world, we are committed to ensuring our team reflects the unique communities around us. We’re ensuring we keep learning by committing to continually revisit and reevaluate our diversity culture.

We encourage applicants across any race, ethnicity, gender/gender expression, age, spirituality, ability, experience and more. If you need any accommodations to make our interview process more accessible to you due to a disability, don't hesitate to let us know. You can learn more here. We can’t wait to meet you.

About Us

At Flowcase, we’re revolutionizing the way companies win business. Our mission? To help clients save time, win more bids, and achieve better results.

As a leading SaaS solution for public tenders, bids, and proposals, Flowcase is trusted by top consulting, engineering, IT, and legal firms in over 35 countries. Our platform streamlines the creation and management of CVs, resumes, and case studies, cutting bid preparation time in half—so teams can focus on what they do best.

With a fast-growing, globally distributed team of 30+ talented and friendly professionals, we’re headquartered in Oslo and have offices in London, Copenhagen, Helsinki, and Toronto. Join us as we continue to expand and make an impact on the future of bidding and proposal management.

Role purpose

Drive and support the company’s ongoing journey within data, digitalisation, automation and business intelligence.

The role combines data analysis, business process improvement, HubSpot development, automation and systems integration. Working closely with Management and teams across the organisation, the role helps turn business needs and data into better processes, improved efficiency and stronger decision-making.

As the main resource in this area, the role offers significant autonomy to identify opportunities, develop initiatives and shape its own agenda, while working in close alignment with Management and the company’s strategic priorities.

Key Responsibilities

Data & Business Intelligence

Develop and improve dashboards, reporting and BI solutions to support Management and business decision-making.
Analyse business data and translate findings into clear, actionable insights.
Establish reliable reporting and data structures across key business areas.
Identify trends, opportunities and areas for improvement through data.
Support Management with ad-hoc analysis and data-driven decision support.

HubSpot & Business Processes

Develop and continuously improve HubSpot as a key business platform.
Design and optimise workflows, processes, automations and reporting within HubSpot.
Improve data quality, structures and processes across the CRM.
Work with stakeholders to understand business requirements and translate them into effective HubSpot solutions.
Identify opportunities to further digitalise and streamline processes across sales, marketing, customer and other business functions.

Automation & Digitalisation

Identify manual, repetitive or inefficient processes that could benefit from automation.
Design and implement automated workflows and solutions across the business.
Continuously evaluate opportunities to simplify processes and improve efficiency through technology.
Support the organisation in adopting new digital tools and ways of working.

Systems & Integrations

Develop and maintain integrations between HubSpot and internal and external software systems.
Work with APIs, integration platforms and data flows to connect systems and reduce manual data handling.
Help ensure data is consistent, accessible and reliable across different platforms.
Collaborate with external software providers and internal stakeholders on system improvements and integrations.

Collaboration & Business Support

Work closely with Management to understand priorities, challenges and opportunities where data and technology can create value.
Collaborate with teams across the company to map processes, understand requirements and implement improvements.
Proactively identify opportunities rather than working solely from predefined requirements.
Communicate insights and technical solutions in a clear and business-oriented way.

Role characteristics

This is a broad and hands-on role sitting at the intersection of Data, Technology, Operations and Business.

While working closely with Management and other teams, the role has the freedom to identify areas for improvement, propose initiatives and shape its own roadmap. The focus is not only on producing analysis, but on turning insights into practical improvements through better processes, automation, systems and data.

The role therefore combines analysis, problem-solving, implementation and collaboration, with the opportunity to have a visible impact on how the company operates and makes decisions.

new_jobs.description:
Our Company
The North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) is a not-for-profit international regulatory authority whose mission is to assure the effective and efficient reduction of risks to the reliability and security of the grid. NERC develops and enforces Reliability Standards; annually assesses seasonal and long‐term reliability; monitors the bulk power system through system awareness; and educates, trains, and certifies industry personnel. NERC’s area of responsibility spans the continental United States, Canada, and the northern portion of Baja California, Mexico. NERC is the Electric Reliability Organization (ERO) for North America, subject to oversight by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) and provincial authorities in Canada. NERC’s jurisdiction includes users, owners, and operators of the bulk power system, which serves nearly 400 million people.

Our Mission
The vision for the ERO Enterprise, which is comprised of NERC and the six Regional Entities, is a highly reliable and secure North American bulk power system. Our mission is to assure the effective and efficient reduction of risks to the reliability and security of the grid.

The Senior Data Analyst, Reliability Assessment, applies technical skill, experience, and subject-matter expertise in the areas of data management and analysis to support the ERO’s efforts to independently assess and report on the overall reliability, adequacy, and associated risks to the interconnected North American bulk power system. This Senior Data Analyst role includes responsibilities to collect, process, and analyze data necessary for assessing risks that could arise from the growing reliance on natural gas for electricity generation, with application to resource adequacy and bulk power system reliability assessments.

The Senior Data Analyst is part of the reliability assessment team that provides superior technical analysis and designs ERO processes for developing and publishing NERC’s reliability assessment reports, including the Long-Term Reliability Assessment and seasonal assessments. The Senior Data Analyst coordinates with the Performance Analysis team to provide reliability assessment information and analysis for the State of Reliability report and the Data and Analytics Integration team on data management, data quality, and analysis.

The Senior Data Analyst, Reliability Assessment, reports to the Manager, Reliability Assessments.

Make use of available datasets containing generation, load, transmission, and natural gas fuel supply information to augment NERC’s collected data in analyzing trends and emerging risks to electric reliability.
Proactively identify and suggest solutions to technical analysis and data problems.
Develop working knowledge of the fundamentals of NERC Reliability Assessments.

Support internal coordination with the Performance Analysis, Event Analysis, Engineering, Standards, and Compliance teams, as needed.

Source and integrate data from Tulip MES, NetSuite ERP, Rippling, SharePoint/Excel, and the enterprise data lake, consuming curated silver and gold layers and working with data engineering on the bronze/silver/gold (medallion) design.

How to Apply

A cover letter and resume are required for consideration for this position; include the cover letter as the first page of your application. The letter should specifically address your interest in this position and outline relevant skills and experience.

Job Summary

The Demography of Aging, Disability and Care Program (DADC) in the Survey Research Center at the Institute for Social Research (ISR) conducts research focused on the consequences of population aging. The program provides leadership for several research projects including the National Health and Aging Trends Study (NHATS) and the National Study of Caregiving (NSOC).

We are seeking a full-time social science data analyst intermediate to collaborate with DADC research faculty to conduct analyses related to population aging, disability and care. The successful candidate will specialize in quantitative social science and have experience working with population-based aging-related surveys, like the National Health and Aging Trends Study (NHATS) and the National Study of Caregiving (NSOC) or similar national surveys.

This is a two-year term limited position with the possibility of extension. An extension will be based on available funding and performance. This position will report to the DADC program director.

Responsibilities*

The job functions of this role will include, but are not limited to:

35% Preparing survey data and creating analytic files

Writing programs to clean, recode and handle missing survey data using statistical packages such as Stata or R.
Prepare and organizes data files for statistical analysis.

35% Performing statistical analyses

Uses a variety of statistical methods and models. Selects and runs statistical tests in consultation with research faculty. Includes weighted analysis of descriptive data and model estimation, including generalized linear models (e.g., linear, logistic, and count regression), survival analyses, and mixed models. Advanced techniques like machine learning methods that may require deeper knowledge of R or Python are also of interest.

30% Documenting procedures and preparing methodological and technical materials

Clearly documents decisions including analytic file construction, variable generation, and model estimation.
Collaborate with research faculty to contribute technical material to publications and presentations. May include descriptions of data and methods, including design decisions, sample size justification, and analytic approach, and well-notated tables and figures.

Required Qualifications*

Master's degree in social science or public health field (e.g., epidemiology, quantitative sociology, demography, health services), or related field.
2-3 years of relevant work experience with complex, population-based surveys including demonstrated data management skills and experience preparing data for analysis and solid grounding in statistical theory and application to social sciences.
Highly motivated, organized, detail-oriented person with excellent multi-tasking ability and record-keeping.
Must be able to program, manage data, and conduct statistical analyses using statistical software packages such as Stata or R.
Willingness to learn and apply new methods and approaches.
Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, including ability to document complex data management and statistical work and excellent interpersonal skills.

Desired Qualifications*

Experience with the National Health and Aging Trends Study (NHATS) and National Study of Caregiving (NSOC)
Demonstrated interest in aging, health, caregiving or long-term care research.
Experience working with interdisciplinary research teams.

Positions that are eligible for hybrid or mobile/remote work mode are at the discretion of the hiring department. Work agreements are reviewed annually at a minimum and are subject to change at any time, and for any reason, throughout the course of employment. Learn more about the work modes.

Work Locations

Work location is expected to be onsite in Ann Arbor with flexibility for hybrid work within our overall Center guidelines.

The Institute for Social Research (ISR) at the University of Michigan seeks to create a community of respect and authentic collaboration by recruiting and retaining individuals that represent a variety of voices as a reflection of our commitment to serve the people of Michigan, to maintain the excellence of the university, and to ground our research in varied disciplines, perspectives, and ways of knowing and learning.

Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact.

A Day in the Life

Peripheral Vascular Health (PVH) is a dynamic business with annual revenue exceeding $1 billion across multiple high-growth therapy areas. PVH focuses on diagnosing and treating diseases of the peripheral arteries and veins, helping patients restore blood flow and reduce the risk of limb loss and other serious complications. The portfolio includes minimally invasive technologies such as drug-coated balloons, stents, atherectomy, thrombectomy, embolization, vein ablation, and embolic protection, designed to address complex peripheral vascular disease across a range of patient anatomies. By combining innovation, clinical evidence, and physician partnership, PVH aims to improve procedural outcomes and quality of life for patients worldwide.

At Medtronic, we bring bold ideas forward with speed and decisiveness to put patients first in everything we do. This position is remote to enhance our competitive edge and expand our cross-functional collaboration efforts. This role will require 10% of travel to enhance collaboration and ensure successful completion of projects.

The Senior Health Economics & Outcomes Research (HEOR) Analyst
will be a critical contributor on the Cardiovascular HEOR team. The Senior HEOR Analyst is responsible for providing analytical and methodological expertise to support the development and execution of global health economic and outcomes evidence for Cardiovascular products, with an emphasis on the Peripheral Vascular Health portfolio. This position may be called upon to support multiple therapies, with a specific focus area on leading the execution of studies using administrative data to generate regulatory-grade evidence.

Role and Responsibilities:

Designs and conducts studies using administrative health care claims data and device-derived data to assess outcomes, health services utilization, treatment patterns and costs associated with the use of PVH therapies. Analysis may be used to support evidence development, federal and global agency (FDA, CMS, EU MDD/MDR) requests, clinical trial design, and reimbursement market trends.
Designs and conducts observational and economic research studies that provide value, perspective and evidence for clinical and/or pre-clinical product portfolio decisions, marketing, regulatory agency submissions, and product reimbursement strategies.
Compares and evaluates the value of products and therapies with the clinical, economic, and quality of life outcomes data from clinical trials and/or epidemiology studies, registries, observational studies, modeling, surveys, and meta-analysis.
Prepare observational and economic research study results for dissemination via abstract, presentation, and/or peer-reviewed publication.
Develops country specific evidence to meet requirements for optimal reimbursement coverage and usage.
Works closely with Reimbursement staff to determine the global economic evidence needs and potential impact of evidence on therapy coverage, payment, and adoption.
Works with clinical research to add relevant health outcomes and economic endpoints to clinical trials and biostatisticians to analyze and report study results.

new_jobs.title: Insights Senior Research Analyst
new_jobs.description:
About Crossroads

Crossroads Church is a growing multi-site, interdenominational church. Our sites are currently located in Ohio and Kentucky, with plans to expand to additional cities. We also have an online presence that serves thousands of people who aren’t located near one of our physical sites.

We believe the story of Jesus' redemption is the greatest story ever told, and that's why we embrace creativity, adventure, authenticity, and tenacity to share this story with the world.

Our desire is to model our staff and church community after the church in Revelation, where people of all nations, tribes, and tongues are worshiping and working together. We’re not there yet, but it’s what we’re working toward with every hire and every person who walks through our doors.

Job Summary

The Senior Research Analyst leads projects and independently delivers quantitative and qualitative insights on key ministry questions and initiatives. They work with the broader Research and Insights Team to serve as a strategic consultant to other Ministry Leaders helping them uncover insights about their products, services, and community members. They will own volunteer relationships and are responsible for helping lead how Crossroads innovates on our current ministry model. This Senior Research Analyst role has a focus on new product/program innovation and will have a great impact on Crossroads’ strategy.

Have significant research experience and a track record of leading teams? We’d welcome your application and may consider you for the Insights Research Manager role.

Principal Duties And Responsibilities

Analyzes data to inform strategic ministry choices, making those ministries more effective.
Develop new and actionable research approaches to answer key ministry questions.
Produce documentation, trainings, reports, presentations, etc. for methods and projects.
Advise and consult other ministry teams on their research objectives and educate them on the appropriate qualitative and quantitative research methods.
Perform research tasks, both quantitative and qualitative, from client consultation to research design to delivery.
Influence strategy initiatives with key partners including Marketing, Site Teams, Site Support, and Leadership Team.

Education Requirements

Bachelor's Degree in Marketing, Psychology, Economics, Statistics, Business, or other related field.
Basic Requirements: 5+ years experience with primary research (quantitative and qualitative) required.

Experience/Skills Requirements

Experience and strong skills in implementing a variety of quantitative and qualitative research methods such as: surveys, interviews, A&U, segmentation, conjoint, focus groups, ethnographies, brand health, and Voice of the Customer programs.
Proficient in creating appropriate sample compositions for research surveys.
Experience with product innovation frameworks and processes as well as user experience testing.
Understanding of research and data tools including: Qualtrics, Decipher, Excel, SPSS, JMP etc.Ability to create methods and deliverables that do not have organizational precedent Able to work with and lead volunteers as they make themselves known to the Crossroads Insights Team.
Must commit to expectations detailed in the “I Promise” document, including using the Bible as the ultimate standard of truth, practicing spiritual disciplines, and pursuing personal purity.

Physical Requirements

Performs effectively under pressure and against strict time constraints.
Must be able to work in common office conditions (sitting at a desk, working on a computer for 60 minutes at a time, etc.).
Desired Qualifications: 8+ years experience with primary research (quantitative and qualitative).
Proficient in advanced quantitative research methods (weighting, tabulation, statistical modeling, etc.)

Scheduling/Travel Requirements

Typically 9am-5pm M-F, but some nights and weekends required Travel outside of Cincinnati rare, but possible.

Crossroads Staff Qualities

Qualities All Staff Teammates Should Exhibit

Mission Oriented: Committed to the Crossroads mission and expectations in the staff “I Promise” document, including using the Bible as the ultimate standard of truth, practicing spiritual disciplines, tithing, and pursuing personal purity.
Availability: Expected to work outside of “normal” schedule for All Hands on Deck high-impact events (Holy Week/Easter, Super Bowl, Christmas, others as needed), participate in all-staff meetings, day of solitude, offsites, etc.
Authenticity: Communicates clearly, directly, and honestly, even under stress, and does so with a sustained positive attitude and demeanor.
Personal Leadership: Envisions, energizes, and enables others to operate at full potential.
Collaborative Self-starter: Thrives as an individual contributor and works well on a team.
Proactive Problem Solver: Takes initiative to understand departmental objectives, adapts to changing and fluid environments, and proactively solves problems.
Humility: Puts others above self and takes ownership of mistakes.
Learner: Desires growth and learning from others.
Flexibility: Able to quickly shift between projects as organizational direction and needs change, able to successfully balance competing priorities.

Crossroads Church is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

GS-12:

Combination: Combinations of successfully completed post-high school education and experience may be used to meet total qualification requirements for the GS-11 grade level ONLY and may be computed by first determining the applicant's total qualifying experience as a percentage of the experience required for the grade level; then determining the applicant's education as a percentage of the education required for the grade level; and then adding the two percentages. Only graduate education in excess of the amount required for the next lower grade level may be used to qualify applicants for positions at grade GS-11.

new_jobs.title: Senior Creative Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
Join us in bringing joy to customer experience. Five9 is a leading provider of cloud contact center software, bringing the power of cloud innovation to customers worldwide.

Living our values everyday results in our team-first culture and enables us to innovate, grow, and thrive while enjoying the journey together. We celebrate diversity and foster an inclusive environment, empowering our employees to be their authentic selves.

At Five9, we believe every customer interaction should be effortless, connected, and on brand. To help us deliver on that vision, we’re hiring a Senior Creative Project Manager—a detail-obsessed, process-driven project manager who shepherds creative and content projects from kickoff to delivery and is often the last set of eyes on an asset before it goes live — ensuring every asset reflects our visual identity and brand voice.

In this role, you’ll manage the day-to-day execution of creative and content assets—coordinating across teams, optimizing workflows, and serving as the final checkpoint for both visuals and messaging. You’ll review creative and content for accuracy, consistency and alignment with Five9 tone, voice and style guidelines, and route issues back to the right owner to fix. You’ll partner closely with content and creative teams while managing and continuously improving the intake, tracking and workflows that bring it all together.

This is a hands-on, senior individual contributor role for someone who brings equal parts operational discipline and creative judgement — and who understands that great brand experiences depend on both.

We are focusing on AI tools across the team, and this role will help us use them well, safely, and on brand.

Key Responsibilities

Own and improve creative request and production processes, identifying opportunities to streamline intake, prioritize competing requests, enforce intake standards and scale output
Coordinate creative workflows across design, content, video and web teams, including internal stakeholders, external freelancers, agencies and vendors — moving work from brief to delivery with consistency and efficiency
Own the creative project calendar and team capacity plan, track progress, and proactively communicate milestones and updates
Serve as the final quality checkpoint before assets go live: review creative (layout, typography, color, logo and brand usage, file specs) and content (accuracy, grammar, tone, terminology, links, and claims) against brand and style guidelines, and route corrections back to the owner
Maintain QA checklists by asset type (web, email, video, social, print, events) and log recurring errors to improve quality upstream
Confirm required approvals (brand, legal, product, regional) are complete and documented before final release
Manage creative projects from intake through delivery, including campaigns, brand assets, content, video, web, and social
Create and maintain clear project timelines, status trackers, and schedules
Serve as the day-to-day point of contact for creative work: tracking briefs, deliverables, reviews, and approvals
Consolidate stakeholder feedback, resolve conflicting input, and manage versioning and final approvals with a clear eye for detail and quality
Identify bottlenecks early, escalate risks and suggest solutions to keep work moving
Lead creative calls, check-ins, and debriefs when needed
Keep stakeholders in the loop without overloading the creative team
Capture lessons learned in project debriefs and keep process documentation, templates, and QA checklists current
Use AI tools like Claude to speed up everyday work such as briefs, status updates, QA checks, and process documentation
Review AI-assisted content and visuals with the same care as everything else, checking for accuracy, tone, and brand fit before anything goes live
Test new AI tools, share what works, and help build prompts, templates, and simple guidelines for using AI responsibly on the team

Key Qualifications

Deep understanding of creative workflows and asset production across digital, print, video, and event channels
Sharp editorial instincts and a strong eye for copy and design quality (typos, inconsistencies, off-brand elements, broken links, incorrect specs)
Familiarity with brand voice, tone, and style guides—and the confidence to help others follow them
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills—able to move work forward while keeping everyone in the loop
Track record of identifying and implementing process improvements that boost team efficiency and content quality
Ability to prioritize competing requests, manage team capacity, and diplomatically push back on scope creep and late changes
Working knowledge of project management methodologies (Agile, Kanban, or hybrid); PMP, CAPM, or similar certification a plus
Comfortable reviewing, proofreading and editing content created by others and giving constructive feedback that builds trust and elevates work
Advanced proficiency in Monday.com for project tracking and working familiarity with SharePoint, Figma, Slack, and Microsoft products; experience with proofing or DAM tools is a plus
Understanding of graphic design fundamentals (layout, typography, color, and file formats)
Excellent organizational and time management skills; strong communicator who works well with creatives and stakeholders alike
Calm under pressure, flexible with shifting priorities, and always two steps ahead
A team player who cares about process, quality, and the people doing the work
Hands-on experience using AI tools like Claude in daily work, including writing clear prompts and getting reliable results
Familiarity with AI image and video tools, and good judgement about when AI helps and when a person needs to take over

Requirements

7+ years of experience in creative project management or content operations, including 4+ years in a dedicated project management role, preferably in B2B SaaS, tech, or agency environments
Bachelor degree or equivalent
Experience managing budgets and opening/maintaining Pos
Experience working in or with an in-house creative team or agency, including vendor management and agency collaboration
Demonstrated experience enforcing brand guidelines, managing file versioning, and running creative approvals Must be able to work Pacific Time, 8 AM–5 PM
We are focusing on AI tools, and Claude knowledge is a must

Work Location: This role is fully remote for candidates who reside outside the 30 mile radius of one of our offices. For candidates who reside within a 30 mile radius of one of our offices, this role is Hybrid and would require 3 days a week (T, W, TH) in office.

As part of our continued commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion, Five9 supports pay transparency during the entire recruitment process. Actual compensation packages are based on several factors that are unique to each candidate including, but not limited to: skill set, depth of experience, certifications, and specific work location. The range displayed reflects the minimum and maximum target for new hire salaries for the job across the United States. Your recruiter can share more about the specific compensation package during your hiring process.

Additionally, the total compensation package for this position may also include an annual performance bonus, stock, and/or other applicable incentive compensation plans.

Our total reward package also includes:

Health, dental, and vision coverage, beginning on the first day of employment. Five9 covers 100% of the employee portion of the health, dental and vision coverage and shares a high portion of the dependent cost. We also offer Short & Long-Term Disability, Basic Life Insurance, and a 401k saving plan with employer matching
Access to an innovative mental health support platform that offers personalized care and resources in areas such as: therapy, coaching and self-guided mindfulness exercises for all covered employees and their covered dependents
Generous employee stock purchase plan
Paid Time Off, Company paid holidays, paid volunteer hours and 12 weeks paid parental leave

$82,300—$229,500 USD

new_jobs.title: Program Manager, M&A Integration
new_jobs.description:
About Us

Ethos Risk Services is a leading insurance claims investigation and medical management company committed to providing better data that translates into better decision-making for our clients. We are at the forefront of innovation in our space, and our success is driven by a dynamic team passionate about delivering exceptional services to our customers.

Job Summary

Ethos' Product Management team is seeking a full-time Program Manager, M&A Integration (REMOTE)
to own acquisition integration from end to end. Every company we acquire brings systems, data, and people that need to be absorbed quickly and cleanly. This role owns the planning, the acquired-company relationships, the execution, and the escalations, and turns each migration into a repeatable playbook so every integration after it is faster and less costly. The role also coordinates cross-team dependencies across four product lines, maintains the portfolio view of initiatives, milestones, and risks, and delivers concise executive status reporting.

Our ideal candidate is a seasoned program manager who has run M&A integrations or large-scale system migrations and is comfortable starting with an ambiguous mandate and closing it themselves.
There is no formal PMO at Ethos today, so the practices this person builds become it. This is a high-autonomy role for someone who manages complex, multi-stakeholder programs with minimal oversight and can distill status into one page an executive can act on.

Key Responsibilities

Integration Ownership - Own acquisition integration programs end to end, including scoping, planning, timelines, resourcing, risk management, and delivery.
Acquired-Company Partnership - Serve as the primary point of contact for acquired-company stakeholders through migration, managing communication, expectations, and change management.
Playbook Development - Codify each migration into a repeatable integration playbook with templates, checklists, data-migration runbooks, and lessons learned, so integration costs decline over time.
Portfolio Management - Coordinate cross-team dependencies across four product lines and maintain a portfolio view of initiatives, milestones, and risks.
Executive Reporting - Produce concise executive-level status reporting and escalate only true decision points, with options and a recommendation attached.
Process Improvement - Identify and remove process bottlenecks and establish lightweight program-management practices that add speed, not overhead.

Qualifications

Education:
Bachelor's or Master's degree in business, management, or a related field (preferred). Equivalent professional experience may be a substitute for higher education/

Experience

Minimum of 7 years of program or project management experience (required).
Minimum of 2 years running M&A integrations, large-scale system migrations, or comparable multi-stakeholder programs (required).
Experience with data and systems migration programs (required).
Experience with claims, healthcare, insurance, or similarly regulated data (strong plus).
Background in insurance, workers' compensation, medical case management, or healthcare services (preferred).
Experience standing up program-management or PMO practices from scratch in a growing company (preferred).
Familiarity with product-led organizations and agile delivery (preferred).

Certifications

PMP, PgMP, or equivalent certification is welcome but not required. Results matter more than credentials.

Skills

Demonstrated ability to own a complex program independently, from ambiguous mandate to delivered outcome, with minimal oversight (required).
Strong stakeholder management, including experience working with external or newly acquired organizations (required).
Excellent written communication, with the ability to distill program status into one page an executive can act on (required).

Working Conditions

This is a remote position based in the United States, working in a home office environment. The role requires frequent prolonged periods of a stationary position and constant operation of a computer and other office productivity equipment. Occasional travel is required.

new_jobs.title: Business & Transformation Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
At Franklin Templeton, we believe success is built through powerful partnerships. As a forward thinking asset manager, we build dynamic relationships with clients, understand their goals, and navigate complex markets together. We leverage cutting edge strategies and deep insights to unlock opportunities for long term wealth creation. Our talented, global teams bring expertise that is both broad and unique.

From our welcoming, inclusive, and supportive culture to our globally diverse business, we offer opportunities not only to help you reach your potential, but also to contribute to our clients’ success.

About The Department

The Enterprise Business Strategies & Implementation team serves as the execution engine for Franklin Templeton's most important strategic priorities. Working directly with the Co-Presidents, Executive Leadership Team, and senior business leaders, the team shapes and drives complex enterprise initiatives that advance the firm's strategy. Team members act as trusted advisors and transformation leaders, partnering across Investment Management, Distribution, Technology, Operations, Legal, Compliance, Finance, Marketing, Human Resources, and Corporate Services to solve complex business challenges, influence decisions, and deliver measurable strategic outcomes. Employees gain direct exposure to executive leadership and the opportunity to lead work that shapes the future of a global asset manager.

How You Will Add Value

Enterprise Strategy & Execution

Lead the execution of the firm's highest-priority business strategies and enterprise initiatives.
Translate executive vision and strategic priorities into clear roadmaps, decisions, and measurable outcomes.
Advise executive sponsors, challenge assumptions, and drive timely decisions at the highest levels of the firm.
Develop recommendations and decision frameworks for executive leaders navigating complex business opportunities and challenges.
Anticipate business risks, opportunities, dependencies, and enterprise-wide impacts before they affect delivery.

Enterprise Program Leadership

Lead complex business transformation programs, applying consulting-style problem solving, executive advisory skills, and strategic decision support from strategy through execution.
Establish governance, decision-making, and accountability models that enable senior leaders to act quickly.
Independently lead multiple high-impact initiatives with limited oversight and competing priorities.
Evaluate business, operational, financial, legal, regulatory, and technology implications through an enterprise lens.
Create momentum, remove barriers, and drive execution with urgency, sound judgment, and disciplined follow-through.

Executive Partnership

Serve as a trusted strategic advisor to executive leadership and senior business stakeholders.
Develop concise, decision-oriented executive communications, recommendations, and briefing materials.
Lead executive workshops, strategic planning sessions, and governance forums that move decisions forward.
Develop and communicate informed points of view, challenge assumptions constructively, and drive executive decisions.

Cross-Functional Leadership

Build strong partnerships across functions, businesses, and regions to advance enterprise priorities.
Influence executives and senior leaders without direct authority, including when viewpoints or priorities differ.
Create alignment across complex stakeholder groups and translate competing perspectives into a clear path forward.
Promote accountability, transparency, collaboration, and enterprise-minded decision-making.

Change Leadership

Lead the people and business dimensions of enterprise transformation and organizational change.
Operate effectively through ambiguity, independently determine next steps, and maintain momentum.
Quickly develop expertise in unfamiliar business topics and structure ambiguous challenges into actionable recommendations.
Identify opportunities to strengthen operating models, governance, efficiency, and enterprise execution.

What Will Help You Be Successful In This Role

Extensive experience leading large-scale business strategy, transformation, or enterprise initiatives.
Demonstrated experience advising executive leadership and influencing senior-level decisions.
Experience independently leading cross-functional initiatives across complex, matrixed organizations.
Management consulting, corporate strategy, business transformation, or comparable enterprise leadership experience strongly preferred.
Strong business acumen and the ability to quickly understand unfamiliar issues, form a point of view, and recommend action.
Exceptional executive communication, relationship-building, and stakeholder management skills.
Proven ability to influence without direct authority, challenge constructively, and drive accountability through execution.

Technical Skills

Business strategy development and enterprise program leadership.
Executive advisory, decision support, and senior-level communications.
Business transformation, operating model, and strategic initiative execution.
Organizational change leadership and stakeholder alignment.
Enterprise governance, risk assessment, and decision-making frameworks.
Financial analysis, business case development, and outcome measurement.
Structured problem-solving and consulting methodologies.
